items.title: NCCIA arrests Faisalabad man for alleged Saudi visa fraud via TikTok
items.description: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) said on Thursday it has arrested a suspect in Faisalabad for allegedly defrauding citizens through a TikTok account advertising visas for Saudi Arabia. A case has been registered against the suspect, who allegedly “used fabricated documents and transferred fraudulent proceeds into bank accounts in collaboration with other” co-suspects, the agency said on X. NCCIA said it recovered two mobile phones, 10 fake SIMs, an Easypaisa account and an alleged merchant account during the operation. “Strict legal action will be taken against those using social media platforms to rob citizens on the pretext of overseas jobs and visas,” NCCIA Director General Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi said in a statement issued by the agency’s spokesperson. He also urged citizens not to transfer money without verifying visa offers on social media and to immediately report any suspicious account to NCCIA. According to the agency’s statistics for 2026 , financial fraud remains the most widely reported cybercrime, constituting 48 per cent of all received complaints. On Oct 10, NCCIA arrested 281 suspects, including 21 foreign nationals and 20 women, during operations against seven illegal call centres allegedly involved in financial fraud, online harassment and honey-trapping in Lahore. In September, NCCIA, along with the Federal Investigation Agency, arrested six suspects involved in cyber fraud and financial scams, illegal money exchange and human trafficking across Punjab.

items.title: 2027: Opposition has no alternative to Tinubu’s policies — Olabimtan
items.description: — Says president has laid foundation for better tomorrow By Dayo Johnson AKURE — The Director-General of the Ondo State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Victor Olabimtan, has challenged opposition presidential candidates to present credible and practicable alternatives to the policies and programmes of President Bola Tinubu’s administration ahead of the 2027 general election. Olabimtan, who is also the Ondo State Coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA), said opposition candidates had yet to demonstrate how they intended to govern differently or improve on the current administration’s policies. He spoke days after the inauguration of the Ondo State PCC, insisting that Nigerians should assess the Tinubu administration based on its achievements, prevailing challenges and prospects for the future. “None of those aspiring to challenge the President has presented convincing and workable templates demonstrating what they intend to do differently or better if given the opportunity. “Instead, they continue to recycle familiar rhetoric without offering practical solutions,” he said. Olabimtan maintained that the Tinubu administration had taken significant steps towards addressing the country’s challenges and laying the foundation for sustainable development. He identified economic management, infrastructure development, education and youth empowerment as areas in which the administration had recorded what he described as significant milestones. According to him, the country’s current economic realities should be considered alongside the situation before the administration’s reforms and the prospects for future improvement. “The ongoing electioneering campaign should not be judged solely by where we are today. Rather, it should be assessed against three critical realities: where we were before now, where we are at present, and where we are heading. “We all know that we are not yet where we ought to be, but we are equally conscious of the fact that we have moved considerably beyond where we used to be. All indices point to the prospect of a better tomorrow,” he said. The PCC director-general said Tinubu had laid a foundation for a better future, particularly for young Nigerians, adding that the President had promised a second term focused on shared prosperity. “What is required of us now is to support and vote for him for a second term so that he can consolidate the gains already recorded and complete the good work he has started,” Olabimtan said. On the preparedness of the campaign council, which was inaugurated on Saturday, October 17, 2026, he said it was committed to mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election and the election of all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the state. He said the council was working to secure support for APC candidates contesting seats in the National Assembly and the Ondo State House of Assembly. “Our mission goes beyond delivering Ondo State massively for President Tinubu. We are equally determined to ensure that all APC candidates, from the State House of Assembly to the National Assembly, emerge victorious with unprecedented margins. “We are working towards this objective, and with the structures and strategies already in place, we are confident of a strong performance in 2027,” he said. Olabimtan commended Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, who also chairs the state PCC, for providing the structures and support required to strengthen the council’s operations. He said the council was confident that its mobilisation efforts would help it secure support from voters who, according to him, appreciated Tinubu’s achievements and commitment to national development. The PCC director-general also urged APC leaders, stakeholders and independent campaign groups across Ondo State to work together, warning that internal disagreements could undermine the party’s electoral objectives. “This is a clarion call on APC leaders and independent campaign groups in Ondo State to join hands with Mr Governor and the Ondo State PCC in the overall interest of our party. “We stand to gain more when we work together. Disagreements are inevitable in politics, but past differences should not be allowed to undermine our collective progress. This is the time to work as a united team rather than at cross-purposes,” he said. Under the campaign mantra, “One Party, One Message, One Campaign Mobilisation,” Olabimtan urged party members to set aside their differences, strengthen their grassroots structures and coordinate their mobilisation efforts. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Ondo State had recorded significant support for Tinubu and expressed confidence that the APC would seek to sustain and improve on that performance in 2027. He urged residents to continue supporting Tinubu and the APC, arguing that continuity would enable the administration to consolidate its reforms and development programmes in education, infrastructure, economic growth and youth empowerment. Olabimtan reaffirmed the PCC’s commitment to working with party leaders, stakeholders and grassroots mobilisers across the state to pursue the APC’s objectives in the 2027 general election. The post 2027: Opposition has no alternative to Tinubu’s policies — Olabimtan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sénégal : la grève générale se poursuit à une semaine des JO de la jeunesse
items.description: La greve generale de 72 heures se poursuit le 22 octobre au Senegal. Lance la veille a l'appel du Front syndical pour la defense du travail (FSDT), le mouvement vise a obtenir une amelioration des conditions de travail dans plusieurs secteurs. Le collectif, qui rassemble 13 organisations syndicales, s'est felicite d'une premiere journee « bien suivie », malgre une mobilisation variable selon les professions. a Dakar, les perturbations ont notamment affecte les transports en commun. Une grande partie des bus publics est restee au depot de la societe nationale de transport, compliquant les deplacements des usagers. Certains ont exprime leur mecontentement face aux difficultes rencontrees pour rejoindre leur destination. La mobilisation a egalement ete observee chez des agents de l'administration municipale. Pour certains grevistes, le mouvement est necessaire pour attirer l'attention sur les revendications des travailleurs, alors que le Senegal s'apprete a accueillir les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ), du 31 octobre au 13 novembre. Un agent municipal en greve a estime que l'organisation de cet evenement sportif, qui mobilise des moyens financiers importants, ne devait pas se faire au detriment du respect des travailleurs. Il a appele a privilegier le dialogue plutot que l'intimidation. Des requisitions contestees par les syndicats Le mouvement n'a toutefois pas ete suivi de maniere uniforme. Dans l'enseignement, certains personnels ont choisi de ne pas participer a la greve, estimant que les precedents mouvements n'avaient pas permis d'obtenir des resultats durables. Dans les transports, les autorites ont pris des mesures pour assurer la continuite du service public. Apres la requisition d'agents de la Senelec, la compagnie nationale d'electricite, le gouverneur de Dakar a annonce le 21 octobre la requisition de certains conducteurs de la societe publique de transport Dakar Dem Dikk. Cette decision a suscite la contestation du FSDT. Son coordonnateur technique, Pape Birama Diallo, a denonce une mesure qu'il juge abusive et accuse les autorites de chercher a entraver le mouvement social. Il a neanmoins affirme que la plateforme restait ouverte au dialogue. La greve doit se poursuivre jusqu'au 23 octobre, alors que Dakar s'apprete a accueillir les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, dans un climat social toujours tendu.

items.title: Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO
items.description: The World Health Organization’s Africa chief warned on Thursday that the continent now faced a “complex” Ebola outbreak after the virus crossed from east Africa to Nigeria, which has reported the first case in the west of the continent. “We are facing a more complex outbreak landscape. Nigeria has confirmed an imported case of Ebola virus disease,” Mohamed Janabi, the regional director for WHO in Africa, told an online media briefing. Nigeria on Tuesday announced an imported case of the Bundibugyo strain behind a major DR Congo outbreak, in a woman, a diplomat who had a history of travel to Uganda. The continent’s most populous nation is the fourth African country affected by the outbreak, which this week came to span the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since October 6. The case reignited memories of a widespread outbreak in 2014 that struck several countries in the region and killed more than 11,000 people across west Africa between late 2013 and 2016. Nigeria’s experience in successfully containing the Ebola outbreak in 2014 raised confidence that the country can respond effectively to new public health threats. The DRC’s Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country’s history, killing 4,381 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases since mid-May, according to the health authorities. The post Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghanaian boxers draw first-day byes at 2026 IBA Africa Elite Championships
items.description: All three of Ghana’s boxers have drawn byes on day one of the 2026 IBA Africa Elite Men’s and Women’s Boxing Championships in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Amadu Mohammed (bantamweight, 55kg), Ebenezer Ankrah (lightweight, 60kg) and Joseph “Jaguar” Commey (light welterweight, 63.5kg) will not fight on the opening day of the competition on Thursday, October 22. The championships have attracted a record 171 boxers, comprising 132 men and 39 women, making this the highest participation in the history of Africa’s premier boxing event. The turnout surpasses the 148 entries recorded at the 2024 Africa Elite Championships, which were also hosted in Kinshasa. That edition featured 101 male boxers and 47 female competitors. Seven bouts are scheduled to open the competition on Thursday as the championships get underway in the Congolese capital. Ghana will be hoping its three representatives can make a strong impression as the tournament progresses, with Commonwealth Games medalist Mohammed competing in the bantamweight division, Ankrah in the lightweight category and Commey in the light welterweight class.

items.title: Inquiétude en France face aux taux d’intérêt à 5%
items.description: Le rendement de l'obligation assimilable du Tresor a dix ans a franchi le seuil symbolique des 5 %, alimentant les craintes sur le coût de la dette et la capacite du pays a redresser ses finances publiques. Un cap franchi et des alertes a repetition Mercredi 21 octobre, le taux auquel la France emprunte sur dix ans a atteint 5,005 % en seance, avant de se stabiliser autour de 4,99 %. C'est une premiere depuis juillet 2002. L'ecart avec le Bund allemand, reference de la zone euro, s'est creuse a pres de 158 points de base, le plus large depuis la crise des dettes souveraines de 2011. La France emprunte desormais plus cher que l'Italie. Une donnee qui n'a pas echappe aux agences de notation, notamment a Fitch, qui a fait savoir que la note de Paris pourrait se degrader si la dette continuait de grimper . Devant l'Assemblee nationale, le 21 octobre, le ministre de l'Action et des Comptes publics David Amiel a averti : « Il y a un moment dans la discussion que nous avons […] il faut prendre le sens de ce qui est en train de se passer […] a un moment nos debats doivent prendre en compte la realite de ce qui se passe. » Le ronron est mortifère. Les taux d’intérêt dépassent les 5% et pourtant on a à l’Assemblée les mêmes débats que d’habitude, le même refus des économies ! Écoutons ce qui se passe à l’extérieur, réveillons-nous ! https://t.co/Vy5GpR5mpt — David Amiel (@Amiel_David_) October 21, 2026 L'envolee s'inscrit dans un contexte tendu. Les violences du 17 octobre ont renforce la defiance des investisseurs, deja inquiets face au deficit public et aux debats budgetaires difficiles. Sur X, l'economiste Marc Touati a tire la sonnette d'alarme : « ALERTE ROUGE : France : le taux d'interet des obligations d'etat a 10 ans vient de depasser les 5 % ! Du jamais vu depuis le 10 juillet 2002 ! Preparez-vous au pire ! » ALERTE ROUGE : France : le taux d'intérêt des obligations d'Etat à 10 ans vient de dépasser les 5 % ! Du jamais vu depuis le 10 juillet 2002 ! Préparez-vous au pire ! Explications et prévisions dans ma vidéo YouTube : https://t.co/LGI3u5oyNN #France #faillite #emeutes #crise #dette — Marc Touati (@MarcTouati) October 21, 2026 L'economiste insiste aussi sur la dependance croissante aux investisseurs etrangers, qui detiennent pres de 60 % de la dette francaise. « On est en train de perdre notre souverainete financiere », a-t-il declare, soulignant un « mouvement de panique » sur les marches. Le precedent gouverneur de la Banque de France, Francois Villeroy de Galhau, avait deja mis en garde en mai , puis son successeur Emmanuel Moulin debut octobre : sans assainissement des finances publiques, la France risquait d'etre « etranglee par les taux d'interet ». Moulin appelle a « rester maîtres de notre destin ». Le 14 octobre, la presidente de la Banque centrale europeenne Christine Lagarde affirmait que « la solution se trouve d'abord en France » . La charge de la dette pourrait depasser 90 milliards d'euros en 2027, selon le projet de budget. Au-dela des comptes publics, la hausse des taux de reference menace de rencherir les credits immobiliers et les prets aux entreprises.

items.title: Overdependence on gold, cocoa leaves Ghana exposed to changes in global commodity prices – ISSER
items.description: The Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) has stated that the dependence on gold and cocoa leaves Ghana exposed to changes in global commodity prices and production conditions. The country’s external position strengthened considerably in 2025, with export earnings growing much faster than imports. The merchandise trade surplus widened from US$3.8 billion to US$13.8 billion, while the current account surplus rose from US$1.6 billion to US$9.4 billion. International reserves also increased, strengthening the country’s foreign exchange position, while the cedi appreciated against major international currencies. However, ISSER expressed worry in its 2025 State of the Ghanaian Economy Report that the improvement was heavily concentrated in primary commodities, particularly gold and cocoa. Minerals accounted for 68.2% of merchandise exports, highlighting continued export concentration. It explained that although non-traditional exports grew by 30.7%, Ghana’s export base remained relatively undiversified. “A strong trade surplus does not necessarily indicate that the economy has become more diversified or internationally competitive”, it warned. Policy Priorities ISSER called for diversification of exports through expand manufactured and processed exports to reduce commodity dependence. Similarly, it wants increased domestic value addition that is the strengthening of processing capacity and linkages between agriculture, mining and domestic industry. Finally, it urged the country to build external resilience via sustain reserve buffers and the strengthening of export competitiveness while reducing vulnerability to commodity price fluctuations.

items.title: Futsal : la CAF salue le quatrième sacre africain du Maroc
items.description: Vainqueur de l’Angola (5-2) en finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de futsal 2026, disputée à Rabat, le Maroc a décroché son quatrième titre continental. La CAF souligne la domination des Lions de l’Atlas, désormais sacrés pour la troisième fois consécutive. Le Maroc continue de régner sur le futsal africain. La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a salué le sacre des Lions de l’Atlas, vainqueurs de l’Angola sur le score de 5-2, mercredi soir à Rabat, en finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de futsal « Maroc 2026 ». Grâce à ce succès, la sélection nationale conserve son titre et remporte la compétition pour la quatrième fois de son histoire, après ses sacres de 2016, 2020 et 2024. Elle devient ainsi la première nation à inscrire quatre fois son nom au palmarès de l’épreuve et signe un troisième sacre consécutif. Dans son compte rendu, la CAF a mis en avant la prestation des hommes de l’équipe nationale devant leur public. La rencontre s’est accélérée en fin de première période. Othmane Idrissi a ouvert le score pour le Maroc à la 17e minute, avant l’égalisation angolaise signée João Campangola une minute plus tard. Youssef Jouad a rapidement redonné l’avantage aux Marocains, à la 19e minute. Au retour des vestiaires, les Lions de l’Atlas ont consolidé leur avance. Idriss Raiss El Fenni a inscrit le troisième but à la 21e minute, puis Ismail Amzal a creusé l’écart à la 33e minute. Deux minutes plus tard, Bilal Bakkali a porté le score à 5-1, plaçant le Maroc dans une position favorable. L’Angola a réduit l’écart à la 37e minute grâce à Anderson Fortes, sans toutefois parvenir à renverser la situation. La sélection marocaine a conservé son avantage jusqu’au coup de sifflet final, déclenchant les célébrations dans les tribunes. Malgré sa défaite en finale, l’Angola termine la compétition à la deuxième place, au terme d’un parcours remarqué, marqué notamment par sa remontée face à l’Algérie en demi-finale. L’Égypte a, de son côté, décroché la troisième place après une large victoire contre l’Algérie (8-1), mercredi, lors du match de classement. Ce quatrième sacre confirme la place du Maroc parmi les grandes puissances du futsal africain. Avec trois titres consécutifs et une nouvelle victoire devant son public, la sélection nationale poursuit une série de succès qui renforce son statut de référence sur le continent. The post Futsal : la CAF salue le quatrième sacre africain du Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Cameroun : formation annoncée de 12 510 jeunes pour l’entretien des infrastructures communales
items.description: © DR L’annonce est du ministre de la Décentralisation et du Développement local Georges Elanga Obam. Le projet entend mettre à la disposition de 139 communes la ressource humaine qualifiée pour pallier le déficit. Pour les années 2026 et 2027, 139 communes du Cameroun verront s’améliorer leurs ressources humaines en vue de l’entretien et de la maintenance de leurs infrastructures. Le gouvernement envisage de former 12 510 jeunes dans les régions de l’Adamaoua, du Sud-Ouest, du Nord-Ouest, de l’Est, de l’Extrême-Nord et du Nord pour augmenter la disponibilité des ressources humaines qualifiées dans ces communes. Les formations seront dispensées par dans des Sections artisanales et rurales et sections ménagères (SAR/SM). Elles porteront sur les domaines comme la maçonnerie, l’électricité, la plomberie, la menuiserie, la réparation des équipements solaires et des ouvrages hydrauliques. Organisées en partenariat avec le ministère de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle, ces formations ciblent 8 340 jeunes en 2026 et 4 170 jeunes de plus en 2027. La formation va se déployer une fois que les protocoles d’accord entre les communes, le Projet gouvernance locale et les communautés résilientes (PROLOG) et les établissements de formation finalisent les protocoles d’accord. Le projet de formation des jeunes vise à renforcer les compétences locales dans les matières concernées en facilitant l’insertion professionnelle de ces jeunes. Ces compétences font parfois défaut aux communes favorisant la dégradation de certaines infrastructures. L’initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du PROLOG, un projet destiné à la construction des infrastructures communautaires et à l’amélioration des services de base. Cet article Cameroun : formation annoncée de 12 510 jeunes pour l’entretien des infrastructures communales est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Que sont-ils devenus ? Après Demba Camara, un regard sur le légendaire Bembeya Jazz National
items.description: Dakar, jeudi 5 avril 1973. La Guinée en particulier et l’Afrique en général, plongées dans une consternation sans nom, venait de perdre, à la suite d’un accident de la circulation survenu au virage du « Phare des Mamelles », le dragon de la chanson africaine, Aboubacar Demba Camara. C’est un géant de la musique africaine et guinéenne qui s’est éteint, laissant le célèbre Bembeya Jazz National en plein succès, amputé de sa plus grande valeur. Dans cette douloureuse situation, l'inquiétude quant à la poursuite des œuvres et au maintien de la consécration s’est transformée en une équation à plusieurs inconnues. Pour sortir de cette impasse, le choix exigeant et difficile du continuateur ou remplaçant de Demba Camara demeure l’inconnue majeure de cette équation. Elle se pose aux hommes de feu Hamidou Diaouné (chef d’orchestre) et tourmente à plus d’un titre le public mélomane. C’est ainsi que la recherche d’un successeur infaillible, de la trempe du « Dragon de la chanson africaine », s’est imposée au Bembeya Jazz National comme un objectif primordial dans le combat pour le prolongement de son triomphe sur la scène musicale guinéenne et continentale. L’itinéraire couronné de gigantesques exploits de cette formation musicale est certes l’œuvre d’un collectif de talentueux artistes, mais il fut singulièrement marqué par un homme, un animateur fulgurant à la voix captivante : le regretté Aboubacar Demba Camara. Pour la succession de Demba, le choix s’est finalement porté sur feu Nagnamory Kouyaté (paix à son âme), à l’époque chanteur de l’orchestre 22 Band de Kankan. C’était une lourde mission à accomplir et une éminente responsabilité à prendre, quand on sait ce que personnifiaient le nom et les œuvres de Demba. C’est dans la salle de spectacle du Palais du Peuple, costumé dans le style de l’empereur du Wassoulou, l’Almamy Samory Touré, que Nagnamory fera sa première apparition lors du concert « Regard sur le passé » . Il était très attendu et est apparu particulièrement décontracté, imitant par la voix et le geste le célèbre Demba Camara. Tout au long de ses prestations ce jour-là, et aux dires des nombreux spectateurs interrogés ayant assisté à ce spectacle, cet élégant griot a donné une parfaite chair de poule à ce public curieux qui avait fait le déplacement jusqu'au Palais du Peuple. L’imitation était au rendez-vous et d'une très belle facture. Mory est donc rentré par la grande porte. Il appartenait dès lors au Bembeya de juger des aptitudes du jeune Kouyaté pour choisir entre la continuité dans l’imitation et la valorisation des véritables empreintes artistiques de Nagnamory Kouyaté. Il était évident aux yeux de tous que le choix de la première option risquait de replonger le Bembeya dans une situation de stagnation. Demba était inspiré ; il avait un cachet tout particulier, difficile à égaler et impossible à surpasser. C’était un génie. Face à ce constat, le Bembeya se prononcera en faveur d’un nouveau virage : une toute nouvelle orientation sous une nouvelle formule qui réunira, autour du doyen Salifou Kaba, deux autres chanteurs : Nagnamory Kouyaté et Moussa Touré, alias J.B. De nouveaux accords relaient les précédents. Le Bembeya change de registre musical : les chœurs prennent le dessus sur les chants en solo, la section cuivre bien déployée rappelle néanmoins les envolées mélodieuses de feu Clément Dorégo, tandis que les doigtés endiablés du charmant guitariste Sékou Bembeya soutiennent une section guitare bien fournie. De l’offensive au lance-roquettes amorcée par la troupe de feu Hamidou Diaouné et menée par le trio Ambiance Bazooka , résulteront indiscutablement de brillantes conquêtes, redonnant confiance et stabilité à cette formation nationale, désormais engagée à défendre et maintenir sa renommée internationale. Depuis cette mutation, de riches répertoires vont meubler le parcours musical du Bembeya. Il se réinstallera, bien que d’une manière différente de la première époque, dans le cœur des mélomanes nostalgiques acquis à sa cause. Le Bembeya Jazz, avec le trio Ambiance Bazooka , produira deux albums ( Le Défi et La Continuité ) à travers des chansons comme « Sinamusodyu » , « Kukuwé » , « Téléphone » , « Dyadya » , entre autres, et brillera encore de mille feux avant de connaître une seconde reconversion au niveau de la section vocale. Entre 1982 et 1983, une autre ossature vocale, s'appuyant toujours sur le pilier qu'était feu Salifou Kaba, émergera pour donner une nouvelle formule au Bembeya Jazz National. Il s'agit du recrutement de deux jeunes chanteurs qui avaient déjà fait leurs preuves : l’un au sein des Sofas de Camayenne et l’autre au sein du Manden Kono de Siguiri. En appui à la section vocale, feu Youssouf Bah et Sékouba « Bambino » Diabaté apporteront un sang neuf au Bembeya par de nouvelles compositions musicales et par la reprise de plusieurs titres qui avaient fait le succès de chacun dans sa formation d’origine. Bambino annoncera son arrivée avec le titre « Télégramme » , tandis que le morceau « Yigui » (la confiance) sera la toute première plongée de feu Youssouf Bah dans le grand bain. Ils débuteront ensemble leurs carrières internationales au sein du Bembeya Jazz National à partir de 1985 au festival d’Angoulême, puis à travers une longue tournée européenne. Ils réitéreront leur participation à ce festival d’Angoulême en 1987 et en 1989, toujours en compagnie du Bembeya Jazz International. Plusieurs albums (près d’une dizaine, y compris les albums solo de guitare de Sékou « Bembeya » Diabaté) seront fignolés par le Bembeya dans sa nouvelle course vers le sommet de la musique africaine contemporaine. Le Bembeya réussira encore à imposer de nouvelles sonorités musicales qui franchiront avec succès les frontières guinéennes. « Won béré » , « Baba Dabiya » , « Fémara » , « Gbapié » , « Sabu » , « Nyanya » , « Golèn » , entre autres, hisseront encore plus haut la renommée de la formation, qui comptait alors un nombre restreint de membres fondateurs. Tout au long de son parcours, entre 1982 et 2015, l’effectif de l’orchestre connaîtra plusieurs mutations dans toutes ses pupitres, renforcé par une équipe de musiciens pétris de talent (Kova Bavogui, feu Mazo, Alpha Camara, Ibrahima Soumano « RDA »…). Plusieurs décès seront enregistrés au sein du Bembeya Jazz National et affecteront le groupe, qui se verra contraint de procéder à de nouveaux recrutements. En 2000, au retour de Paris après l’enregistrement de leur dernier album, un différend oppose le Bembeya à feu Youssouf Bah et Kova Bavogui, ce qui conduit à l’exclusion des deux musiciens. Si Youssouf Bah réintégrera plus tard les rangs après de nombreuses négociations, Kova Bangoura, droit dans ses bottes, quittera définitivement le Bembeya Jazz National. C’est à la suite de cette exclusion et du départ de nombreux autres musiciens que le groupe procédera à de nouveaux recrutements pour la promotion de son nouvel album. La composition de l’orchestre se présentait alors comme suit : Section guitare : Sékou Diabaté « Bembeya » (guitare solo), Mamady Kouyaté « Dyélikè » (guitare rythmique), Dyeli Kani Madou Diabaté (guitare accompagnement), Aziz Dyelidji Diabaté (guitare basse). Section cuivres : feu Mohamed Asken Kaba (chef d’orchestre, trompette), Maître Barry Mamadou Aliou (saxo alto et soprano), feu Clément Dorégo (saxo ténor et soprano). Section rythmique : feu Papa Kouyaté (tumba et djembé), feu Mory Mangala Condé (batterie). Section vocale : feu Salifou Kaba, feu Nagnamory Kouyaté, M’Bemba Camara. A la suite du rappel à Dieu du chanteur Youssouf Bah dans la nuit du 14 au 15 juillet 2015, plusieurs autres interprètes défileront au sein du pupitre chant (Rizo Bangoura, Dambakaté…), aujourd'hui dirigé par Almamy Labass Sylla. Depuis lors, sous la houlette de Sékou Diabaté « Bembeya », force est de reconnaître la constance de cet ensemble national, qui continue d'évoluer tant bien que mal dans la capitale et parfois à l’étranger lors de tournées. Sékou « Bembeya » Diabaté a su assurer progressivement la relève au sein de cette formation. Alors qu'il entend s’éloigner prochainement de la scène, il gratifiera le public guinéen de la dédicace d’un album chant intitulé « I tolomalon » , composé de plus d’une dizaine de titres. Le Bembeya Jazz National, dans sa version 2026, se présente sous la composition suivante : Sékou Diabaté « Bembeya » (guitare solo) Sidy Diabaté (1ᵉʳ accompagnement) Bakary Kanté (2ᵉ accompagnement) Kalil Keita (guitare basse) Moriba Kaba (batterie) Lamine Condé (congas) Abdoulaye Fanyé Touré (saxo ténor, trombone) Fodé Salifou Camara (trompette) Salifou Camara (trompette) Cheick Abdoul Kader Bah (trompette) Almamy Labass Sylla (chant) Mohamed Kourouma (chant) D’ambitieux projets animent cette nouvelle équipe rajeunie qui, dans un nouvel élan, est prête à conquérir d’autres sommets de la musique guinéenne et continentale. L’une de leurs premières ambitions est la réalisation d’un nouvel opus composé de 9 titres, incluant un morceau instrumental à la guitare de Sékou Diabaté « Bembeya ». Cet album comportera notamment la reprise de 5 anciens succès du Bembeya ( Camara Musso , Mami Wata , Mobèni Bara , Sènèro , N’Na Fatoumata ) ainsi que 4 nouvelles compositions. Sur ce chemin du retour, le Bembeya rencontre toutefois d’énormes difficultés d’ordre financier (moyens de transport, salle de répétition, réalisation de clips vidéo, commercialisation du concert Regard sur le passé enregistré en versions anglaise et espagnole) qui méritent d’être prises en considération. Pour assurer son renouveau, le Bembeya a encore besoin du soutien du gouvernement – qui a déjà doté l’ensemble d’un lot d’instruments modernes- , des mécènes et des personnes de bonne volonté, afin de réaliser ses rêves : ceux de revaloriser la culture guinéenne, qui prend ici un nouvel envol. Bon vent au Bembeya Jazz National, et vive la culture guinéenne !

items.title: ANPS Awards 2026 : Ismaïla Sarr, Saly Sarr, Sa Thiès…voici les meilleurs sportifs de la saison
items.description: L'Association nationale de la presse sportive du Sénégal (ANPS) a rendu public, ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026, le palmarès de la saison 2025-2026 des meilleurs sportifs sénégalais. Le verdict est tombé à l'issue du dépouillement des bulletins, organisé le matin même dans les locaux d'Eric Favre TV, à la Cité des Eaux. Football, athlétisme et lutte se partagent les principaux trophées. Ismaïla Sarr, roi des Sénégalais de l'étranger Le Trophée Jules François Bocandé, qui distingue le meilleur footballeur sénégalais évoluant hors du pays, revient à Ismaïla Sarr. L'attaquant de Crystal Palace totalise 164 points et devance le gardien Édouard Mendy (Al-Ahli, 108 points) ainsi que Sadio Mané (Al-Nassr, 103 points). Sa saison justifie ce large succès. Sacré champion d'Afrique avec les Lions, il a aussi soulevé la Ligue Conférence avec son club, dont il est le meilleur buteur avec neuf réalisations. Il y ajoute un Community Shield et 26 buts toutes compétitions confondues. Au Mondial 2026, ses quatre buts en ont fait le meilleur buteur africain du tournoi. Saly Sarr, une domination écrasante Chez les femmes, le Trophée Amadou Dia Bâ de la meilleure sportive de l'année revient à Saly Sarr. Avec 300 points, la triple sauteuse laisse très loin derrière elle Cheikh Thiam (boxe savate, 96 points) et Oumy Diop (natation, 77 points). Son année a été exceptionnelle : l'or en Diamond League et à l'Ultimate Championship, le bronze aux Championnats du monde, un titre de championne d'Afrique, et un nouveau record du Sénégal établi à 15,08 mètres. Moustapha Guèye, pilier de la défense de Teungueth FC Le Trophée Ibrahima Coulibaly, réservé au meilleur footballeur du championnat sénégalais, va à Moustapha Guèye. Le défenseur de Teungueth FC cumule 136 points, devant Abdourahmane Mbodji (Génération Foot, 128 points) et Mouhamed Diop (AJEL, 91 points). Titulaire à 30 reprises, il a été l'un des artisans du titre de champion de son équipe, dont la défense n'a concédé que six buts en 30 journées. Il est également élu meilleur défenseur de Ligue 1. Sa Thiès devant Franc, grâce à sa victoire sur Modou Lo En lutte avec frappe, le trophée Manga 2 sourit à Sa Thiès, de l'écurie Double Less. Il rassemble 213 points, devant Franc (182 points) et Reug Reug (89 points). Sa victoire retentissante sur Modou Lo, alors Roi des arènes, a largement pesé dans ce choix. Ngagne Sène réussit le doublé En lutte sans frappe, Ngagne Sène conserve le Trophée Abdourahmane Ndiaye Falang pour la deuxième année consécutive. Le lutteur de l'écurie Kaye Bakh de Rufisque obtient 196 points. Capitaine de l'équipe nationale, il compte deux médailles d'or au Tournoi de la CEDEAO, une autre aux Championnats d'Afrique de lutte olympique, et 13 finales remportées sur 16 disputées. Ce palmarès met à l'honneur aussi bien les Sénégalais de l'étranger que les acteurs du championnat local et les athlètes des autres disciplines. Les lauréats seront célébrés officiellement lors du gala des ANPS Awards, prévu le 12 décembre à Dakar. O.B.N

items.title: We toured Karachi's Red Line to bring you this update
items.description: Few things test Karachi commuters’ patience like its roads and public transport. For nearly five years, construction of the Red Line has added another obstacle to daily journeys, with traffic diversions, dust and disrupted businesses along the corridor. We wanted to understand why the project was taking so long. So we travelled the route, documented the work on the ground and spoke to the people living and working beside it. The idea for the Red Line was born in the early 2010s when it was clear Karachi could not survive its own traffic. The Japan International Cooperation Agency, known globally as the sensei of city surveys, was asked to help. It counted the cars and motorcycles and studied the madness before coming up with a simple plan: Make six Bus Rapid Transit corridors. BRT, as it is called, is a short form for giving buses their own lane in the middle of the road where no other vehicles can enter. This allows the bus to zoom people up and down a road without being hemmed in by pesky lane-violators. One of the six corridors, the Red Line, ran from Numaish near Quaid-e-Azam’s Mazar to Malir Halt, a little further after the Karachi airport. This 26.6km strip is Karachi’s busiest and includes University Road. The planners gauged that it would need over 260 electric buses for it. “We found that more than 60 per cent of regular commuters cross Numaish every day,” said Zubair Channa, CEO of TransKarachi, a public sector company in charge of the project. Back in 2011, that looked like up to 166,000 vehicles a day at the busiest intersections surveyed on the corridor. Roughly half to two-thirds of them are motorbikes and rickshaws, with just 5pc buses. Project timeline The Red Line work began in March 2022 and is less than half done more than four years later. Documents of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), a major financier, note April 30, 2027, as the loan closing date. According to the Asian Development Bank’s project data sheet , the four financiers had disbursed approximately $128.93 million by August 20, 2026. ADB had disbursed $87.63m of its $235m loan, while the French Development Agency and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank had disbursed $21.38m and $19.92m, respectively, out of $71.8m each. No disbursements had been recorded against the Green Climate Fund’s combined $49m grant and loan commitments. For a project of such scale, two years of inconvenience is a given, said Channa. TransKarachi estimates the corridor work will be done by December 20, 2026. It said other components of the project will be completed progressively. The Malir Halt Depot is targeted for completion by April 2027, while the Bagh-e-Karachi Depot is expected to be completed by July 2027. The remaining structural and station works are targeted for completion by June 2028. The Red Line has been divided into two lots or batches. The first is a 9.4km stretch from Malir Halt to Mosamiyat with six stations and two bus depots (at Malir Halt and Bagh-e-Karachi). The contract was awarded to Zahir Khan & Brothers (ZKB) for Rs13.8 billion. The company’s key projects include Swat Motorway, Lahore Eastern Bypass, and New Jam Sadiq Bridge in Karachi. The company was also previously involved in the construction of mass transit, such as the Islamabad-Rawalpindi and Multan Metro Bus systems and the Lahore Orange Line Metro and depot. ZKB began work on Red Line’s Lot-1 on May 10, 2022 and had an initial completion deadline of May 9, 2024, which was later extended to June 30, 2026. The second lot covers a 12.85-kilometre stretch with 16 stations and was awarded to China Railway No. 3 Engineering Group-AM Associates (joint venture) on January 4, 2022, for Rs15.93bn, and construction commenced on August 15 of the same year. The original completion deadline was August 14, 2024, which was later extended to June 30, 2026. Per its website, AM Associates earlier also worked on the 19.21km Hazara Motorway and the Kohala–Muzaffarabad road for the National Highway Authority. On April 21, 2026, TransKarachi terminated its contract with China Railway No. 3 Engineering Group–AM Associates for Lot-2, citing slow progress, unsatisfactory performance and violations related to health, safety and the environment. The contractor challenged the decision in the Sindh High Court, which referred the matter to the contract’s Dispute Resolution Board. The board subsequently declared the termination “unlawful and invalid”, finding that it had been hasty and had failed to adequately account for the project’s complexity. It also identified shortcomings on TransKarachi’s part, including its failure to provide complete designs and an unobstructed work site — factors that contributed to delays. The dispute therefore went beyond disagreements over the contractor’s performance: it also raised questions about the project authority’s own contractual obligations and how the stalled works would be completed. After the termination, the Sindh cabinet approved off-budget emergency funding and directly engaged the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) under a government-to-government arrangement to stabilise the corridor and restore essential infrastructure, i.e. mixed traffic lanes, service roads, and drainage along Lot-2. FWO took over the site in May 2026 and is scheduled to complete the assigned works by the end of the year. The contract for the remaining works—structural works and BRT station works—is in the tendering process and procurement will take place through ADB Open Competitive Bidding. According to the bank, the method “facilitates open competition among all eligible bidders” through advertising to provide an equal opportunity to as many qualified bidders as possible. “The lowest bidder gets the contract,” said Rehan. Bids for the replacement Lot-2 structural works had been submitted on October 8 and were being evaluated, with a contract award expected within about a month. Delays TransKarachi gave a number of reasons for the delay in the project: post-Covid inflation, land acquisition for bus depots, design revisions, and delays in utility line relocation. There is no justification for it, said Channa, but he reiterated the position that inconvenience caused by a project meant to provide long-term respite to Karachiites was meant to be. The people directly affected by work on the corridor described the ‘inconvenience’. “This construction work has been going on for more than 3.5 years. Initially, it was very slow but has picked up speed over the last two months. The dust is the worst part … because of the construction, the traffic jams are bad here. The roadwork has affected our work … there is no work.” — Stallholder, Safoora Chowrangi “Before the construction work began, my stall would be crowded with customers. Now, there is barely anyone. I used to set up my stall on the main road previously, but now we are down here.” — stallholder, Mosamiyat “A project that was supposed to be completed in two years is going on and on and on with no end in sight. Our business has shut down because they have dug up the road right in front of my shop.” — shop owner, University Road “My house is at a 20-25 min distance from here but because of the construction I have been missing my morning classes almost every day. In the evening, our rickshaw is usually stuck in the traffic for an hour or so.” — student, University of Karachi “It is like 60pc of my day is spent in traffic.” — commuter, NIPA According to TransKarachi, people displaced because of the Red Line construction are compensated. The compensation rates vary according to the type and category, from Rs27,500 to Rs302,500. So far, 131 people have been compensated, with payments made during 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Rehan said the displaced people primarily included vendors operating from extended structures and movable pushcarts. “No permanent structures were affected by the project,” he added. TransKarachi also has a Grievance Redress Mechanism in place, where all complaints by commuters, affected communities and other stakeholders along the Red Line corridor are registered. During September 2026, a total of 14 complaints were received, of which the highest were concerning traffic, followed by utility, access, and environment. Depending on the nature of the complaint, Rehan explained, a Corrective Action Plan is prepared, or an appropriate resolution is provided in coordination with the concerned department, project team, or contractor. The relevant stakeholders undertake the necessary actions to address the issue, and progress is monitored through the GRM portal. Once the issue has been addressed, the complainant is informed via email, along with corresponding photographs where applicable, and requested to provide feedback on the resolution.The complainant is subsequently given three days to respond. If no response is received within this period, the complaint is closed in accordance with the approved procedure. Any feedback received from the complainant is documented in the GRM records.

items.title: El petróleo marca máximos desde mayo ante el riesgo de nuevos ataques en el Golfo Pérsico
items.description: El petróleo se ha disparado a los niveles más altos desde principios de mayo, por encima de los 112 dólares por cada barril de brent . A pesar de que el flujo de crudo a través del estrecho de Ormuz crece hasta niveles anteriores a la guerra, el riesgo de nuevos ataques a instalaciones petroleras mantiene los precios altos. Además, Estados Unidos ha ordenado la salida de parte del personal y de familiares de empleados de sus embajadas en el reino, lo que pone de manifiesto la creciente preocupación por una nueva escalada del conflicto regional. Según The New York Times , los ejércitos de Estados Unidos e Israel están elaborando planes para atacar Irán tras las elecciones israelíes de este fin de semana, en una operación que incluiría ataques sobre infraestructuras de energía y arsenales de drones y misiles. Además, un ataque con drones contra el yacimiento de Shaybah, de Saudi Aramco, mató a dos personas, pero no afectó a las operaciones. La empresa ha evacuado sus instalaciones principales. items.title: Targeted by Trump, International Criminal Court wins top EU rights prize
items.description: Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was awarded the European Union’s top rights prize on Thursday, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump. “The European Union is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions, and this prize recognises the important work of the court in upholding international law and justice,” said European Parliament chief Roberta Metsola, announcing the award. The ICC thanked the European Parliament for giving it the Sakharov Prize “at a time when the Court and its officials face unprecedented challenges”. “Against this backdrop, the Sakharov Prize carries particular significance, reaffirming the importance of independent judicial institutions and of those who work to uphold international law,” ICC President Tomoko Akane said. This month, the United States announced sanctions against the ICC aimed at crippling the day-to-day operations of the court, which tries individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”, furious that judges have issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleged crimes in Gaza. The win comes after ex-ICC judge Navi Pillay, who also served as UN rights chief, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize this month — a choice Trump slammed as “ disgraceful ”, arguing the award should have gone to him. The EU has already thrown its support behind the ICC in the face of the US sanctions — which will come into force in six months — and has said it is “ready to take any necessary measures” to make sure the court can keep working. “The International Criminal Court must be free to pursue its mission, independently, and without pressure or intimidation,” EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said on social media after the prize was announced. Brussels is hoping to use the delay before the sanctions are applied to try to talk the US down, but is also eyeing implementing a “blocking statute” to shield the ICC from Washington. Three finalists Set up in 1988 and named after Soviet dissident Andrei Sakharov, the EU prize is bestowed annually on individuals or organisations to recognise their fight for human rights or democracy. The ICC was among three finalists this year, alongside Tanzania opposition leader Tundu Lissu and twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, representing those prosecuted by the Iranian government. The nominees are put forward by the political groupings in the EU, and the winner is chosen by senior lawmakers. An award ceremony will be held in December. Lissu, head of Tanzania’s opposition Chadema party, was detained in April 2025. He faces a possible death penalty if convicted of treason for allegedly inciting the public to boycott elections last year. Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, 21, have respectively been sentenced to death and 36 years in prison for having taken part in anti-government protests in Iran. Other recent high-profile winners of the Sakharov Prize have been Venezuelan opposition chief Maria Corina Machado, deceased Russian Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny and the people of Ukraine.

items.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province. He made the remarks while chairing a meeting of the provincial apex committee in Peshawar, where he arrived earlier in the day on his first visit to the province since the imposition of governor’s rule and the declaration of emergency on Oct 11. The meeting, attended by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, reviewed KP’s overall security situation. Federal ministers and newly appointed provincial advisers were also present. Addressing the committee, PM Shehbaz reiterated that emergency and governor’s rule had to be imposed “under extreme compulsion”. “I promise that we will leave no stone unturned in bringing back the happiness and era of progress to this province, and in the practical realisation of the wishes, aspirations, and dreams of this province’s people that have been shattered due to the worst actions of recent years,” he said. The prime minister affirmed that the Centre “will place all possible resources at your feet”. He added that himself, the Advisory Council led by the governor, the president and the CDF “will ensure that this province, once again, not only matches the other provinces in the race for development, but I would be extremely happy if it moves even further ahead”. The prime minister regretted that “terrorists were summoned back here” after peace had been established, “washing down all sacrifices down the drain”. “There can be no greater enmity with the country than not honouring and respecting such sacrifices, not holding them in esteem,” he remarked, highlighting that young soldiers left their homes and families to defend their country. The premier called for an “all-encompassing analysis as to why this happened”, adding that there was “no worse callousness, criminal negligence, and hostility towards the national interest than this”. He said: “All issues of the people were pushed aside — whether it is education, healthcare, or protecting the lives and property of the people — and [having] matters with terrorists instead. I believe that no other example can be found of such hostility against the country, in terms of their attitudes, detachment, and callousness.” PM Shehbaz asserted that 5,000 police vacancies were not filled, Safe City projects were yet to be completed, the capacity of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) had not been enhanced significantly, and neither were special measures taken regarding police training. He recalled that all provinces had agreed at the time of the 2010 National Finance Commission Award that KP, being the front-line region in combatting terrorism, needed ample resources. “From 2010 to today, more than Rs800 billion in funds have either already been provided or are being provided under this,” he stressed. “However, not only did it resurface, but the weapons needed to counter terrorism, the required capacity, and the trained officers needed were nowhere to be found.” While saying he would not go into the details, the prime minister emphasised that he had assured the provincial governments of ex-chief ministers Ali Amin Gandapur and Sohail Afridi of the Centre’s full support in the fight against terrorism. “But nothing was done regarding this,” he regretted, adding that the government could not remain a “silent spectator” when a “party was stooping to such enmity against the country” and the economy and society were being destroyed. “Therefore, on this occasion we made this one last effort,” the premier said, referring to the province’s interim handover to the federal government under governor’s rule. Highlighting the Centre’s efforts to stabilise the economy over the past two and a half years, PM Shehbaz remarked, “It wouldn’t have been possible [without] unprecedented partnership between political and military hierarchy.” He said the federal government could not remain a silent spectator when “terrorists were roaming around dancing in all areas of KP, and were ruling over some areas in the evening, and collecting extortion” at a time when the stabilisation of Pakistan’s economy was being acknowledged globally. The prime minister recalled the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between the Centre and reiterated that his government was “compelled to make this decision” of imposing governor’s rule. PM Shehbaz remarked that the province was “shattered with wounds due to the circumstances created in the past several years”. He highlighted the poor law and order situation over the past six years, recalling that security forces and law enforcement agencies had made sacrifices to establish peace in KP. The premier said there was corruption of Rs100bn in the clean drinking water of the Cities Improvement Project and Rs37bn in the “infamous looting” in the case about the Kohistan District Accounts Office . He said that “80,000 people were martyred and the [economy] suffered a loss of several hundred billion dollars. Only then, in 2018, was peace completely restored in this country”. Describing the province as “very beautiful”, the premier expressed his hope that the government “work hard day and night and speedily make it progress towards development and prosperity”. “This is the province that is the first extremely strong wall of the homeland,” he noted. Development of merged districts a ‘special priority’ In his address to the apex committee, the KP governor termed establishing peace and stability in KP a “collective priority”, and stressed that it was in the interests of the entire country. Referring to the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said that the peaceful transition showed that the people of the province wanted peace and stability. “I want to pay tribute to my people who showed restraint despite the turmoil,” he said, asserting there had been no untoward incident in the region following the measures. On Oct 14, three days after emergency was imposed, a protest demonstration by PTI workers in Khyber’s Bara tehsil turned violent as protesters clashed with police. Injuries to party workers and cops were reported in the incident. Speaking at the meeting, Kundi also paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in the war against terrorism, including personnel of the police, army, Frontier Corps, and Federal Constabulary. “These sacrifices demand a more effective strategy to combat terrorism,” he underscored. The governor reiterated that the foremost priority of his KP Advisory Council was to restore peace and eliminate terrorism. Kundi termed the development of the merged districts a “special priority”. “The people of these regions have paid a heavy price during this fight against terrorism. Now, they deserve better education, health, and economic opportunities,” he declared. “The federal government’s cooperation in establishing peace and stability in the province is very significant,” the PPP leader highlighted, saying he was keen to play his role in this collective endeavour. The governor maintained that the people of KP would not have to choose between peace and development. “This is our collective responsibility to provide people with both.” Kundi declared that the KP Advisory Council would keep playing its role in integrating these merged areas in the circle of national development. “The public’s trust is the only metric of measuring our success in the war on terror,” he asserted, while reaffirming that the whole network of terrorism would be annihilated, and the facilitators and financiers of terrorists would also be targeted. “I seek constant support and supervision by the federal government,” he asked, expressing the hope that the Centre would continue its cooperation. Emergency amid security challenges The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament last week amid protests by the opposition. Governor Kundi, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, had chaired a meeting of the provincial apex committee a day after governor’s rule was imposed. In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province. Kundi asserted that under the new set-up, tackling terrorism would be the priority. Later that day, Kundi, addressing a press conference, called for greater coordination between the Centre and the province, stressing that policies on counterterrorism will “come from Islamabad [..] not Kabul,” in an apparent jibe at the PTI-led KP government, which has been accused of maintaining a “nexus” with terrorist groups by federal ministers. The Centre’s move to impose governor’s rule and emergency in KP also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI and in opposition at the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, with counterterrorism policy being one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their talks. The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied . It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. Soon after, the Centre also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP. Federal ministers have also alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, stating that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there. Additional input by Irfan Raza

items.title: Golfe : les exportations de pétrole dépassent leur niveau d’avant-guerre
items.description: Malgre les attaques contre les petroliers et les perturbations du trafic dans le detroit d'Ormuz, les exportations de petrole du Golfe ont retrouve, puis depasse, leur niveau d'avant la guerre contre l'Iran. Selon les donnees preliminaires de Kpler, les flux regionaux, hors Iran, ont depasse en moyenne 24,5 millions de barils par jour durant la semaine achevee le 18 octobre, contre environ 24,4 millions durant la semaine precedant le declenchement du conflit, fin fevrier. Ce rebond tient surtout a l'adaptation rapide des producteurs. L'Arabie saoudite a augmente ses exportations via Yanbu, sur la mer Rouge, grâce a l'oleoduc Est-Ouest, tandis que les emirats utilisent davantage leur liaison vers Fujairah, qui debouche directement sur le golfe d'Oman. Les transferts de petrole de navire a navire se sont egalement multiplies au large d'Oman et des emirats. Avant la guerre, environ 17 % du brut regional evitait Ormuz ; cette proportion avoisine desormais 40 %. Loin d'un retour a la normale Le detroit reste pourtant loin d'un retour complet a la normale. Les volumes qui y transitent demeurent inferieurs a ceux d'avant-guerre, tandis que les attaques contre les navires se poursuivent. Mais le recours aux convois proteges, aux itineraires alternatifs et aux transferts en mer a permis de compenser une grande partie des pertes. Cette resilience a cependant un coût. Les primes d'assurance et les tarifs des petroliers restent tres eleves, ce qui rencherit fortement l'acheminement du brut vers l'Asie. Saudi Aramco et ADNOC ont meme dû adapter leurs conditions commerciales pour maintenir l'interet des raffineurs asiatiques. L'Iran constitue l'exception majeure : ses exportations restent pratiquement a l'arret sous l'effet du blocus americain. Le paradoxe est donc saisissant : malgre une guerre toujours active et un Ormuz sous tension, les autres producteurs du Golfe parviennent desormais a exporter davantage de petrole qu'avant le conflit.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Ngaparou, Saly et Malicounda se mettent au vert
items.description: Dans le cadre des préparatifs des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, le directeur général du Cadre de vie, Bouna Seck, a conduit, mercredi 21 octobre, une opération d’embellissement dans les communes de Ngaparou, Saly et Malicounda, dans le département de Mbour. Au programme : plantation d’arbres, installation de bacs à fleurs et mobilisation des collectivités territoriales pour améliorer durablement le cadre de vie. Le département de Mbour se prépare à accueillir les JOJ Dakar 2026. La Direction générale du Cadre de vie a déployé ses équipes, mercredi 21 octobre, dans les communes de Ngaparou, Saly et Malicounda, pour mener des opérations d’embellissement. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la volonté des autorités de rendre les espaces publics plus accueillants à l’approche de cet événement sportif international, prévu pour une première en Afrique. Pour cette journée, une centaine d’agents ont été mobilisés. Au total, 500 arbres-tiges et 500 bacs à fleurs ont été annoncés, avec des palmiers et d’autres aménagements paysagers destinés à embellir les axes concernés. Ces interventions font suite à des opérations de sensibilisation et de désencombrement déjà réalisées dans les mêmes zones. « Nous avons comme objectif de toucher tout le Sénégal. Le Cadre de vie se veut être partout au Sénégal, aussi bien à Dakar qu’au fin fond du pays », a déclaré Bouna Seck, soulignant la volonté de sa direction d’étendre ses actions au-delà de la capitale. Au-delà de l’accueil des délégations et des visiteurs attendus, ces aménagements visent également à améliorer le quotidien des populations locales. Le directeur général a ainsi insisté sur la nécessité d’une appropriation collective des initiatives engagées. « Chaque Sénégalais, chaque riverain devrait être l’ambassadeur du cadre de vie. Chaque Sénégalais devrait se dire que le cadre de vie dépend de moi et commence par moi », a-t-il fait savoir, appelant les populations à préserver les installations mises en place. Si la plantation et l’embellissement constituent une étape importante, leur entretien demeure un enjeu majeur. Bouna Seck a indiqué que des équipes de la Direction générale du Cadre de vie sont mobilisées pour assurer le suivi des aménagements. Il a également invité les collectivités territoriales à s’impliquer davantage dans leur entretien. Les maires de Ngaparou, Saly et Malicounda ont accompagné les opérations et se sont montrés disposés à participer au suivi des installations. Pour les autorités, la réussite de cette initiative dépendra autant des travaux réalisés que de la sensibilisation des habitants et de la pérennisation des aménagements après les JOJ. Ibrhima MBAYE ( Correspondant)

items.title: Ghana’s fiscal consolidation in 2025 largely driven by expenditure restraint, not revenue growth – ISSER
items.description: Ghana’s fiscal consolidation in 2025 was driven largely by expenditure restraint rather than increased revenue mobilisation, the Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER), has disclosed in its State of Ghanaian Economy Report 2025. According to the economic research firm of the University of Ghana, though smaller deficits and lower debt reduce pressure on government financing and create conditions for greater macroeconomic stability, fiscal adjustment achieved through sharp reductions in capital spending may constrain infrastructure development and future growth. It therefore advised that sustaining fiscal consolidation requires not only expenditure discipline but also stronger domestic revenue mobilisation and improved spending efficiency. Ghana’s fiscal position improved substantially in 2025, with the overall deficit narrowing from 7.9% to 1.0% of GDP on a commitment basis and the primary balance returning to surplus. The World Bank similarly estimates a general government deficit of 1.2% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Total revenue and grants amounted to 16.1% of GDP, while capital expenditure declined from 2.5% to 1.4% of GDP, raising concerns about public investment. The public debt also fell from 62.7% to 46.0% of GDP, reflecting fiscal adjustment and the effect of cedi appreciation on the domestic currency value of external debt. ISSER said Ghana’s fiscal consolidation was substantial, but sustaining it will require stronger revenue mobilisation without sacrificing productive public investment. Policy Priorities On policy priorities, ISSER wants the strengthening of revenue mobilisation via the broadening of the tax base, improve compliance and reduce revenue leakages. Again, it called for the protection of productive investment through improve expenditure efficiency while safeguarding priority infrastructure and social spending. It also emphasise on sustaining fiscal discipline, calling for improved commitment controls, the prevention of arrears accumulation and the management of debt refinancing risks.

items.title: Israeli forces arrest cancer patient, daughter returning to Gaza
items.description: Israeli forces arrested two Palestinians on Tuesday evening as they were returning home to the Gaza Strip after traveling to Egypt for medical treatment, according to a statement from their family and one of their relatives who spoke to Mada Masr. The two arrested, a cancer patient and her daughter, were among patients who were traveling both in and out of Gaza via the Rafah border crossing, which was reopened on Tuesday for the first time following its extended three-week closure by Occupation forces . Twenty-nine patients, along with 42 companions, left the Gaza Strip on Tuesday to receive treatment in Egyptian hospitals. Among them were critical cases, chronic disease patients and those with serious injuries. A group of 75 Palestinians returning to Gaza after receiving medical treatment abroad arrived via Rafah the same day to the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis. The Rafah crossing, which was closed for almost two years after Israel occupied the crossing area in 2024, was reopened in February to provide passage to the sick and injured exiting Gaza for medical treatment, those returning from Egypt after completing treatment courses abroad, as well as for Palestinians who were stranded outside the strip and unable to return home amid Israel’s genocidal war. Before they are allowed to return home, returnees must pass through extensive security checks administered by Israeli forces manning the Karam Abu Salem checkpoint. So far, a number of returnees have been subject to arrest at the site. Amal Ghazy al-Rify and her daughter Yasmin Rifaat al-Rify were returning to Gaza on Tuesday after around two years of medical treatment in Egypt, according to Haitham al-Rify, a relative of the two women who lives in Gaza. Rify told Mada Masr that Amal is an elderly woman who was receiving treatment for her cancer, and that her daughter had traveled with her as a companion. They decided to return without completing the medical course as Amal’s health and psychological condition had begun to deteriorate, he said, recalling that she had expressed her desire to return to Gaza despite her illness. “Before she set off on her way back, she said ‘I feel like I’m going to die, and I want to return to die in my country,” he recalled. Describing Amal’s condition as critical, Rify said that she and her daughter had registered their data at the Palestinian Embassy in Cairo in order to return home, and that they had received prior approval for their travel. He condemned their arrest at the Karam Abu Salem checkpoint, stressing that neither is involved in any political or military activities. He told Mada Masr that the family was not informed by any entity about the circumstances of their arrest or their place of detention, adding that they have reached out to the International Committee of the Red Cross for further information but are yet to receive further details. The family appealed in a statement on Wednesday to responsible parties, human rights and humanitarian organizations to intervene urgently to uncover the fate of Amal and Yasmine, to ensure their safety and work toward their release. The two women left Gaza “seeking treatment and hoping for recovery and returned to find themselves facing detention instead of enjoying safety and stability after a tough medical trip,” according to the family’s statement, which added that medical “treatment is a right, dignity is a right and freedom is a right that cannot be infringed upon without a legal justification.” The pair are not the first to be arrested during their return journey back. Before the extended closure of the crossing through October, Occupation forces arrested a young man named Mohamed Jihad al-Shourbajy at the border, prompting the Palestinian Center for the Defense of Prisoners to warn that the crossing was becoming a “trap” for Palestinians returning to their families. At the time, the center questioned the role of the European mission stationed at the crossing and its responsibility for ensuring the safety of citizens transiting through it. Amal and Yasmin have not been allowed to contact their lawyers, the center stated on Thursday, expressing concern about their safety and conditions in custody. It added that their arrest brings the total number of Palestinians arrested at the crossing to seven, stressing that the border has come to represent a risk to travelers and again questioning the role of the European Union delegation at the facility. The European mission has been in place in a technical capacity at the Rafah crossing since its February reopening. They suspended their work half-way through March in protest at another case of arrest. The mission described the March incident as a clear violation of the agreements signed by the parties regulating the crossing’s functioning and ensuring travelers’ freedom of movement. When the crossing opened for two-way traffic in February, Palestinians returning to Gaza were subject to inspections at “Regevim,” a newly established Israeli-run checkpoint several kilometers inside the crossing in Palestinian Rafah. Palestinians subjected to these inspections described them to Mada Masr at the time as “humiliating and degrading,” explaining that they were blindfolded, restrained and interrogated for hours before being allowed to pass. In July, the Occupation moved the checkpoint to Karam Abu Salem, in the strip’s southeast, continuing its inspections there. People returning to Gaza are required to navigate the Rafah crossing, travelling around 50 km east to the checkpoint, before they are finally allowed to enter the strip fully. Israel’s Public Broadcasting Corporation, Kan, cited unnamed sources in July to claim that the move came after the discovery of attempts to smuggle unauthorized goods into the strip, including cigarettes, tobacco and electronic equipment. It claimed that the move would not hinder travelers’ movement and that the checkpoint’s relocation was to improve inspections and ensure the safe and efficient continuation of the crossing’s operation. Regardless, the Occupation has repeatedly closed the crossing, as indicated in a report on border activity in September issued by the Gaza Crossings and Borders Authority. Severe disruptions to movement were evident as the crossing was closed for 20 out of 30 days in the month. Zaher al-Wahidy, information unit manager at the Gaza Health Ministry, said around 30 to 40 patients are able to travel on days when the crossing is open; a tiny fraction of the 21,000 patients, of whom 5,600 are children, who have completed the necessary documents for medical transfer and are waiting inside the strip. Ten patients referred for treatment abroad died during the extended three-week closure as they were not able to travel, Wahidy said, adding that “every day of delay could cost the lives of more patients.” He estimated that around 2,000 patients have died so far as a result of being prevented from traveling for treatment since Israel took control of the Rafah crossing in May 2024. The Health Ministry in Gaza said last week that the crossing’s closure has led to a severe and rapid accumulation of critical medical cases, as waiting lists grow daily, exceeding the capacities of the exhausted and besieged hospitals’ ability to accommodate or provide the minimum standard of treatment. The ministry has called for serious and urgent pressure on Israel to open the strip’s crossings and facilitate the exit of patients in critical condition to save whoever can be saved. Wahidy also emphasised that at least 200 patients should be allowed to travel every day, a step he said would help bring down the medical transfer waiting lists to which tens of people are added daily. With hospitals and medical facilities decimated, and access to equipment and supplies limited by Israeli obstruction of the passage of goods into Gaza, options for treatment inside the strip are severely limited. There is a “total absence of chemotherapy capacity,” Wahidy said, noting that equipment for surgeries is also limited since there is low capacity for diagnostic services through MRI scanning. The Gaza Health Ministry warned on Thursday that limited access to engine oils is threatening hospital operations, which rely primarily on generators, currently at critical risk of “forced and sudden shutdown.” The post Israeli forces arrest cancer patient, daughter returning to Gaza first appeared on Mada Masr .
