items.title: Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr Jean Kaseya, has blamed a lack of international interest for the absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, saying the situation might have been different if the outbreak were affecting Western countries. Kaseya made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he called for greater African investment in vaccine research and manufacturing. He said, “I can tell you, if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccine will already be available. Why this vaccine today is not available? Because some of our partners decided to consider this issue as an African issue, they were not interested.” The Africa CDC chief, however, said the agency was taking steps to address the gap, including supporting clinical trials of vaccine candidates. He disclosed that an African manufacturer in Egypt was conducting clinical trials of a potential vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. Kaseya also said the agency was working with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to explore clinical trials and compassionate use of Ervebo, a vaccine developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola. He stressed that the continent had the expertise and capacity to advance vaccine development, adding that Africa should not continue to depend solely on external partners during public health emergencies. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind. We have the knowledge, we have people with intelligence, we have capacity to manufacture vaccines, and we need to move on,” he said. Kaseya also called for greater domestic funding and improved coordination among African countries and international partners. He said 28 African countries had contributed funding to support the response to the current outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment. The outbreak, declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026, has caused more than 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, according to Congolese health authorities The disease has also been detected in other countries, with the Kenyan Health Ministry reporting a ninth case in the country on Tuesday, prompting concerns over cross-border transmission. Nigeria also confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20. The patient, a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, is receiving medical care, while health authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring. The post Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: President Zardari departs for Germany on 3-day visit to discuss bilateral ties
items.description: President Asif Ali Zardari departed for Germany on Thursday on a three-day visit to discuss bilateral ties as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations. In a statement issued earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”. President Zardari “has departed from Lahore for Germany”, the President’s office said on social media on Thursday. The FO statement highlighted that the visit “holds special significance in the context of the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries being commemorated this year”. It said the visit reflects the “deep commitment of both countries to further strengthening the partnership”. During his visit, President Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as senior leadership and business leaders, with a “particular focus оп economic and trade cooperation”, FO said. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah is also expected to accompany the president on his trip, with the matter being discussed in Murad’s meeting with German Consul General Thomas E. Schultze. In September, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. During the meeting, Germany appreciated Pakistan’s mediation efforts in regional conflicts, especially in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab while the two sides also agreed to “get negotiations on peace for Ukraine going”, according to the German foreign office. Meanwhile, in June, a German delegation announced plans to bring about 30 German companies to Pakistan and link local businesses to European markets.

items.title: Pakistan, EU agree to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation at multilateral forums
items.description: Pakistan and the European Union (EU) have agreed to strengthen cooperation at multilateral forums, including the United Nations, to advance a coherent counterterrorism approach, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday. The agreement was reached during the 10th round of the Pakistan-EU Bilateral Counterterrorism Dialogue, held in Islamabad. The Pakistani delegation was led by Dr Fareha Bugti, director general (counterterrorism), while the EU side was headed by Anna Strazska, the European External Action Service’s special envoy for counterterrorism. During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on recent regional and global developments affecting the terrorism threat landscape and unequivocally condemned terrorism in all its forms, reaffirming their commitment to combating the threat. According to FO, the EU condemned recent terrorist attacks in Pakistan, expressed solidarity with the suffering of affected civilians and recognised the value of Pakistan’s efforts to combat terrorism. “Acknowledging each other’s role in the ongoing global fight against terrorism, Pakistan and the EU expressed concern at the security implications of the situation in Afghanistan,” the statement added. The two sides maintained that effective multilateralism remained essential to building lasting international consensus on terrorism. The discussions also addressed the evolving nature of terrorist threats, including the exploitation of cyberspace and information and energy resources to advance their objectives, the statement said. The FO said Pakistan and the EU exchanged best practices on preventing and countering violent extremism, terrorism financing and radicalisation in all forms, particularly the use of cyberspace by terrorists. It added that the “two sides identified priority areas for cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to regular, institutionalised engagement on counterterrorism”. The FO said the next round of the dialogue would be held in Brussels at a mutually convenient date next year. The dialogue comes as Pakistan’s counterterrorism challenge enters a new and more complex phase, with terrorist groups evolving their methods of financing and recruitment. On Tuesday, an international seminar on Pakistan’s evolving counterterrorism landscape, organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, highlighted the changing methods of terrorist groups, including their financing and recruitment. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar urged the Afghan authorities to take “concrete, verifiable and irreversible action” against the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other groups operating from Afghan soil. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, who also addressed the seminar, cited UN assessments indicating that more than 6,000 TTP fighters were present in Afghanistan, with the overall militant presence exceeding 20,000.

items.title: GES warns teachers against GH¢210 promotion scam
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has warned teachers applying for promotion to disregard demands for GH¢210 from individuals claiming they can facilitate their applications. The Service said it had received reports that some individuals were requesting the money from promotion applicants under the pretext of helping them secure approval. In a notice shared on Facebook on Wednesday, October 21, the GES stressed that the teacher promotion process was fair, transparent and entirely free of charge. It, therefore, urged applicants not to make payments to individuals who claim they can facilitate or influence the outcome of the process. “Applicants are, therefore, advised to ignore any demands and refrain from making payments to individuals who claim they can facilitate or influence the promotion process,” the Service stated. The GES further directed teachers to follow only the official procedures and guidelines communicated by the Service in pursuing their promotion applications. The warning comes amid concerns over attempts by individuals to exploit teachers seeking career advancement by demanding money in exchange for purported assistance. The Service’s advisory is intended to protect applicants from potential financial exploitation and reinforce the integrity of the promotion process. Teachers have been urged to remain vigilant and avoid unofficial payment arrangements, as the GES maintains that no fee is required to facilitate or influence their promotion applications.

items.title: Uganda Airlines enters Ghana aviation market with flights between Entebbe and Accra starting Oct 27
items.description: Uganda Airlines is entering Ghana’s aviation market from October 27 with a promotional return fare flight between Entebbe and Accra, raising the prospect of stronger price competition on travel between West and East Africa. The Ugandan national carrier will begin four-times-weekly services on October 27, 2026 offering travellers an additional option on a market currently served by established airlines connecting through their regional hubs. The promotional fare could put pressure on competing carriers to review their pricing, particularly for passengers travelling between Ghana and Uganda for business, leisure and family visits. Any sustained reduction in ticket prices, however, will depend on demand, available capacity and how rival airlines respond. For Ghanaian travellers, the entry offers a potential opportunity to compare more fares and schedules when planning trips to East African destinations. Businesses could also benefit if lower airfares make regional meetings, trade missions and commercial partnerships more affordable. The route is relevant to efforts to deepen trade between the two regions, where the cost and convenience of air travel can influence how frequently entrepreneurs, investors and service providers meet across borders. Improved connectivity could also support tourism exchanges, giving Ghanaian visitors another travel option to visa-free Uganda while helping Ugandan travellers access Accra’s commercial, cultural and hospitality markets. Uganda Airlines’ entry comes as African aviation stakeholders seek to improve intra-continental connectivity and reduce dependence on indirect journeys through European and Middle Eastern hubs. Better connections are also viewed as important to the African Continental Free Trade Area’s ambitions to increase trade among African economies. The passengers originating their travel from Accra, Ghana, the greater competition could benefit consumers. Ticket are now on sale for the new service which will operate via Lagos, Nigeria.

items.title: ‘No prosecution will ever be possible’ if stay in Hanan Aludiba case stands – Srem-Sai
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai has warned that allowing the Court of Appeal’s decision to suspend the trial of Hanan Aludiba and his wife, Faiza Seidu, to stand could make it easier for criminal proceedings to be halted over objections to charges. In a Facebook post on Thursday, October 22, Dr Srem-Sai disclosed that the Republic had filed an appeal at the Supreme Court challenging the Court of Appeal’s order suspending proceedings at the High Court. He argued that complaints about charges on a charge sheet should not, on their own, be sufficient grounds to stop a criminal trial, especially when the objections have already been dismissed by the trial court. “If the Court of Appeal’s decision is allowed to stand, no prosecution will ever be possible, since all it would take for a trial to be suspended is an Accused Person complaining about anything on the charge sheet,” he said. Dr Srem-Sai added that the state had challenged the order because, in its view, the law did not support suspending a criminal trial under those circumstances. He said the appeal was filed on Wednesday, a day after the Court of Appeal issued its suspension order. The Court of Appeal halted the High Court proceedings on Monday, October 19, pending the determination of Hanan’s appeal challenging alleged defects in the charge sheet. The defence’s objections relate to aspects of the charges brought against the accused persons. The Supreme Court is now being asked to review the suspension order. Its decision will determine the state’s challenge to the stay of proceedings, while the underlying criminal case remains before the courts.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS abuse: Psychiatrist warns of trauma, depression, and suicide risk among affected girls
items.description: A clinical coordinator at the Accra Psychiatric Hospital, Dr Peggy Asiedua Ekremet, has called for immediate psychological support for students alleged to have been sexually abused at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), warning that the experience could have lasting effects on their mental health, education and future relationships. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show , Dr Ekremet said the reported abuse could leave the affected students struggling with fear, shame, guilt, anxiety and other emotional difficulties, with some at risk of developing depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Her comments followed reports of sexual abuse allegedly involving the school’s headmaster. According to information discussed during the programme, 19 girls had complained of sexual assault. Dr Ekremet said sexual abuse could have serious psychological consequences, regardless of whether the victim was a child or an adult. “Whether it’s sexual harassment, rape, whatever, I mean, should never happen to any child or even any adult,” she said. She explained that the immediate response to such an experience could include shock, fear, emotional numbness and, in some cases, a feeling of detachment from reality. These reactions, she said, could develop into what mental health professionals describe as an acute stress reaction, accompanied by sadness, guilt, shame, self-blame, hopelessness and panic. Dr Ekremet warned that the effects of sexual abuse might extend beyond the immediate emotional distress, affecting the girls’ behaviour, relationships and ability to continue with their education. Some victims, she said, might experience flashbacks, intrusive memories and nightmares, while becoming unusually alert to potential threats. She explained that a girl who had experienced sexual abuse could panic at the sound of a door slamming or become frightened simply by hearing a man’s name. Others might struggle to remain in the same space as men, whether they were their peers or older adults. The psychiatrist said the experience could also lead to significant changes in behaviour, including withdrawal from friends and family, increased anger, changes in eating and sleeping patterns, and a loss of interest in school. “Sometimes they can just say that they won’t go to school anymore. Or you would see a decline in their academic performance,” she said. She added that the effects could undermine the girls’ self-image and influence how they approach relationships in the future. According to Dr Ekremet, sexual abuse is a major risk factor for depression, anxiety disorders and PTSD. Some victims might also turn to alcohol, smoking or other substances in an attempt to cope with the distress. In severe cases, she warned, the emotional burden could lead to self-harm and suicidal thoughts. “By the time you realise, somebody has actually ended their life, because they are so distressed that the only thing they can think about is that it may be better if I were not alive,” she said. She said that children and adolescents were particularly vulnerable and needed timely support to prevent their distress from worsening. Responding to a question about whether the affected girls should already be receiving treatment, Dr Ekremet agreed that they needed immediate psychological first aid and continued professional care. She said many hospitals in Ghana now had mental health units, but identified Kumasi as the nearest place to Obuasi where the girls could access a multidisciplinary team to assess and manage their needs. “Immediate response will be to see a psychologist and, if there is a referral to the psychiatrist, for us to see whether it is just therapy they need or some may need a combination of psychological therapy and medication as well,” she said. She said the Ghana Education Service (GES) had guidance and counselling units in schools, which could provide support to students who needed help. However, she said that not every student would feel comfortable approaching a designated counsellor. Some might find it easier to confide in another trusted adult, including a teacher. She urged schools to make it clear that students could speak to trusted adults and report abuse without being blamed or threatened. “Many of us are not raised to speak our minds, but I think that this is a time when we need to let our children know that speaking up will not get you into trouble,” she said.

items.title: Uganda Revenue Authority delegation visits Tema Oil Refinery to study refining operations
items.description: A delegation from the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) has visited the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) to learn about Ghana’s experience in crude oil refining as Uganda advances plans to establish its own refinery. The delegation, accompanied by officials from the Petroleum Commission (PC), visited TOR on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, as part of an information exchange programme in Ghana. TOR’s Managing Director, Edmond Kombat, and Deputy Managing Director, Alhaji Mustapha Batalima Abubakar, welcomed the team and shared insights into the refinery’s operations and business. During the visit, TOR’s technical team briefed the delegation on the refining process, explaining how crude oil is processed into finished petroleum products. The session provided an opportunity for the visitors to gain a better understanding of the technical stages involved in refining, particularly the processing of local crude oil. The head of the delegation, Arthur Musinguci, said the visit would help the team deepen its understanding of the refining process as Uganda progresses with its refinery development plans. He said the delegation was keen to learn from TOR’s operational experience.

items.title: GES mourns four pupils killed in Aboabo Junction accident
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has expressed condolences to the families of four pupils of Mahad Islamic School at Akotosu who died in a road accident at Aboabo Extension Junction in the Ashanti Region. The accident, which occurred on Tuesday, October 20, in the Asokore Mampong Municipality, also left three other pupils injured. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 22, the GES said it had learnt of the incident with “profound sorrow”, describing the deaths as a painful loss to the affected families, the school and the wider education community. READ ALSO: Four pupils killed as van crashes into children in Aboabo The deceased have been identified as Juraid Mohammed, Anisah Ibrahim, Fati Muniru and Raiyan Faisal. The Service extended its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, the management and staff of Mahad Islamic School, and the entire school community as they come to terms with the loss. It also expressed concern for the three pupils who sustained injuries in the accident, wishing them a speedy and full recovery. The GES used the incident to appeal to motorists and other road users to prioritise the safety of schoolchildren, describing them as vulnerable road users who require particular care and protection. “The GES appeals to motorists and all road users to prioritise the safety of our vulnerable schoolchildren at all times,” the statement said.

items.title: America Is About to See What Happens When Voters Turn to AI
items.description: If you were wondering whether AI could make the midterms even more confusing, here’s one data point: Several people who thought they were donating to James Talarico unwittingly gave their money to someone else. Talarico, a Texas Democrat, is running for Senate in what’s probably the most closely watched race of the upcoming elections. Search Google for how to contribute to his campaign, and you might get an AI-generated answer that links to ways “you can chip in securely.” Until a few weeks ago, one of those featured links was actually controlled by an unrelated political-action committee that sent the money instead to the reelection campaign of another Democrat: Senator John Hickenlooper of Colorado. The mix-up wasn’t all AI’s fault. The link led to a misleading donation page that carried Talarico’s name and picture, and specified only at the bottom that the money would go to Hickenlooper. But Google’s AI tool evidently didn’t read the fine print. And perhaps no one would have clicked on it had Google not highlighted the page in an authoritative-sounding AI response. A spokesperson for Hickenlooper’s campaign told me that the Colorado Democrat, whose seat is considered safe, had not intentionally siphoned the donations. Rather, an outside group, the Kitchen Table Values PAC, had created the fundraiser without Hickenlooper’s knowledge. This appears to have fooled at least three people, who donated a combined total of $1,011, the spokesperson said. Rich Wilkins, the Democratic organizer behind the PAC, told me that the money was supposed to be split between Talarico and his group. “If a page was incorrectly going to Hickenlooper, that sounds like a human-error issue,” he said. After a Democratic digital-advertising strategist discovered the misleading fundraiser while Googling his party’s Senate candidates, the page was removed from the fundraising platform ActBlue, and Hickenlooper’s campaign forwarded the misdirected money to Talarico. The 2026 midterms will mark the first federal election in which tens of millions of voters are getting some of their political information from generative-AI tools. In a September survey, the American Association of Political Consultants Foundation reported that 4 percent of respondents had consulted a chatbot such as ChatGPT for election information in the previous month. Far more—nearly 40 percent—reported getting such info from Google’s AI-search summaries. As the election nears, those numbers will surely rise. There’s a reason for AI’s growing popularity with voters: These tools are convenient, and their answers are personalized. In theory, they have the potential to debunk the kinds of corrosive conspiracy theories that flourish on social media; even Grok, Elon Musk’s chatbot, will correctly tell you that Donald Trump lost the 2020 election. But chatbots are already bringing new complications to an internet that has been teeming with political falsehoods and distortions. Between fake-news sites cropping up to influence AI answers, models that are drawing on foreign propaganda, and chatbots dispensing misleading voter information, the age of AI-mediated politics is beginning to feel awfully familiar. [ Read: What Trump’s chatbot told me about the election ] In the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, most chatbots couldn’t search the web, and they were trained to tread cautiously around questions about elections and current events. Today’s AI tools are still instructed not to take sides politically, but they’ve evolved into all-purpose assistants that will answer your election questions directly, confidently—and sometimes wrongly. In a forthcoming report, Forum AI, a start-up that evaluates AI models’ performance on questions about controversial topics, found that about 40 percent of chatbots’ answers to election-related questions contained at least one factual inaccuracy. When Forum’s researchers asked one widely used model when they needed to request a mail-in ballot to vote in the midterms in Pennsylvania, the chatbot said November 3. The actual deadline is a week earlier. (Forum did not specify the precise AI model.) In the same report , shared with The Atlantic ahead of its publication, Forum determined that about one in three responses cited an unreliable information source, such as posts on Reddit or Quora. Google’s Gemini answered a question about why America’s global power is declining by citing an article from People’s Daily , a Chinese state-run news outlet. “These aren’t trick questions,” Campbell Brown, a co-founder of Forum AI, told me. “There’s no excuse for chatbots to keep getting them wrong.” The companies say their bots have improved since Forum conducted its research in August. Over the past two months, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic have all partnered with the nonpartisan nonprofit Democracy Works to pull accurate, up-to-date information about how, where, and when to vote. OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 was the most accurate of the models tested by Forum, and Nate Evans, a spokesperson for OpenAI, told me he believes that the company’s bots should rate higher now. In an email, the Google spokesperson Davis Thompson told me that the company tests its AI answers on election topics “extensively,” and that these responses show up on Google searches only when the company is confident AI can provide good information. A spokesperson for Anthropic, whose integration with Democracy Works launched last week, declined to comment. Chatbots can be uniquely convincing. In a recent report from the Brennan Center for Justice, a nonpartisan think tank, a researcher posed as a Dallas-area real-estate agent who was suspicious of the election process. Claude responded that the feeling of disempowerment was “completely understandable” but insisted that elections aren’t actually run by a “shadowy group of elites” in Washington. The problem is, most people don’t particularly want to be talked out of their beliefs, Gideon Nave, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School of Business who studies AI and cognition, told me. He worries that the same persuasive power that can convince a conspiracy theorist that the moon landing was real could also make AI a potent tool for manipulation of public opinion. “You can implant all sorts of ideas in people’s heads when they’re using AI, and they feel that it’s their own responses.” Inevitably, a cottage industry has sprung up to consult candidates on how to influence what AI says about them. On the left, the advocacy group Run for Something launched a platform called CampSight that monitors what LLMs are saying about an issue or candidate and recommends how to shape those narratives. On the right, the Center for Campaign Innovation has published research on how AI models respond to questions about candidates and the sources they most often cite. “We’re campaigning for the AI vote now,” Eric Wilson, the group’s director, told me. Some of the most effective “sloptimization” tactics are simple, though not always obvious. “Most candidates we talked to were not filling out Ballotpedia profiles,” Jordan Haines, Run for Something’s chief technology officer, told me, referring to the online repository of election information. “They were like, ‘Eh, no one really reads that.’” Most voters may not be visiting Ballotpedia in droves, but it turns out that their chatbots are. LLMs also love websites with dot-gov domains, both Haines and Wilson told me. That could lend an advantage to incumbents, who can use their official House.gov or Senate.gov web pages to seed messaging for chatbots to pick up on. Challengers, though, might find AI answers easier to sway, because there’s often less information about them in the public record. [ Read: Your search results are getting sloptimized ] Official government websites typically don’t draw contrast between candidates or weigh the relative merits of differing views. Yet those are the kinds of questions people are starting to ask AI. To answer them, chatbots can’t always turn to mainstream news outlets; many have put up measures that block AI bots from ingesting their articles without a specific content agreement. ( The Atlantic, for instance, has a corporate content-licensing deal with OpenAI, and otherwise blocks most AI crawlers.) Good sources can be especially scarce for state and local races, Katie Harbath, whose firm, Anchor Change, advises tech companies on policy, told me. To fill those gaps, AI tools may scrounge among iffy sources. Researchers at a cybersecurity start-up called VisionHeight told me that they recently discovered 37 different suspicious websites, all registered on the same night in September, that seem tailor-made to appear in AI answers about elections. The sites carry newspapery names such as the Scranton Beacon and the Tar Heel State Report, but they read nothing like newspapers. Instead they are stuffed with questions and answers about state and local candidates. “Which candidate in MI-04 has the stronger plan for public safety?” asks one page on the Wolverine State Report. Its answer begins: “Sean McCann is the stronger choice,” referring to the Democratic nominee for Congress from that district. At least some of this material is already making its way into AI answers. When I asked Google’s Gemini-powered “AI Mode” Does Sean McCann support defunding the police? , its response drew on and cited the Wolverine State Report and the Kalamazoo Beacon, both of which are part of the network that VisionHeight discovered. The answer in this case was not necessarily inaccurate; his campaign website says he doesn’t. (McCann is just one of many candidates named by the Wolverine State Report, and there’s no reason to believe he had anything to do with the website. His campaign did not not respond to a request for comment.) Thompson, the Google spokesperson, said that “data voids” are long-standing problems for search engines and AI answers alike, and that the company is always looking out for coordinated attempts to exploit them. After I asked him about the network of sites, the sources seemed to stop appearing in search results. And Google’s AI Mode began giving a different answer about McCann’s position: Whether he supports defunding the police “depends on the perspectives of his campaign and his political opponents,” it said. Although it’s unclear who is behind the network of midterm-focused sites, trolls and foreign governments could use similar methods to seed lies for chatbots to regurgitate. According to the Global Disinformation Index, chatbots have already cited a false claim by the Russian defense ministry to wrongly answer a question about Russia’s control of Ukraine. And on Wednesday, NewsGuard, a company that tracks misinformation, reported that Google’s AI answers had picked up on a deepfake video spread by a Russian influence campaign that falsely depicts a student accusing Talarico of sexual assault in 2012. A decade ago, the 2016 election revealed how social media had corroded the political-information sphere. The last thing AI companies want is another Cambridge Analytica : They are rolling out blog posts cataloging their preparations against misinformation and manipulation. “We take the responsibility to deliver high quality, trustworthy information seriously,” Google says, a claim echoed by OpenAI and Anthropic. It’s reassuring that they say they’re taking that responsibility seriously. It just happens to be the same thing the social-media companies have been telling us for years. Victoria Feng contributed reporting.

NAIMOS conducts 738 operations against illegal mining in four months
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says it conducted 738 operational activities between June 13 and September 30, 2026, as part of efforts to combat illegal mining and protect Ghana’s natural resources. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K.S. Appiah, disclosed this during a media engagement, where he outlined the Secretariat’s operational achievements and plans to strengthen enforcement against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. According to him, the operations covered approximately 50,662 kilometres and included reconnaissance, mobile and riverine patrols, special operations and community engagement. He said the interventions targeted illegal mining activities, particularly around vulnerable water bodies, forest reserves and other environmentally sensitive areas. 74 firearms recovered, 1,970 changfan machines destroyed During the period, NAIMOS task forces recovered 74 firearms and 551 rounds of ammunition. They also seized excavators, pumps, vehicles and other equipment allegedly used to support illegal mining. Colonel Appiah said approximately 1,970 changfan machines and 863 makeshift structures had been destroyed. Six suspects were also apprehended and handed over to the appropriate authorities for further investigation and action. “Our responsibility extends to preserving evidence and supporting the justice process so that enforcement can produce credible deterrence,” he said. Bases established to sustain operations Colonel Appiah said the operations were supported by forward operating bases and temporary operating bases established at strategic locations to maintain pressure on illegal mining hotspots and prevent activities from resuming in areas previously cleared. In the Western Region, NAIMOS has established forward operating bases at Iziyama, Asankragua and Agona, with temporary bases at Prestea and Axim, according to the operational briefing. The Enchi base supports operations in the Western North Region, particularly around the Tano and Bia river systems and adjoining forest areas. In the Eastern Region, operations around Akyem Oda were described as being supported by a forward base at Kibi. Bases at Tepa and Manso Nkwanta support enforcement activities and the protection of reclamation sites in the Ashanti Region. Colonel Appiah said NAIMOS had also conducted coordinated operations in the Central, Bono, Ahafo, Savannah and Northern operational areas, working with other security agencies, including the military and police. The Secretariat plans to establish additional forward operating bases in 2027 to expand its operational reach and improve its response to emerging illegal mining activities. Environmental recovery remains a priority Colonel Appiah said the long-term objective was not simply to disrupt illegal mining but also to secure water bodies and forest reserves and support environmental recovery. “Measurable environmental improvement remains an essential test of long-term success,” he said. He stressed that sustained enforcement and follow-up operations would be necessary to prevent illegal miners from returning to areas where their activities had been disrupted. NAIMOS says the effectiveness of its operations will ultimately depend on whether cleared areas remain protected and environmental conditions improve over time.

items.title: NAIMOS targets galamsey equipment suppliers, facilitators in renewed crackdown
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says it will intensify efforts to target the equipment suppliers and facilitators who support illegal mining, as it seeks to sustain cleared areas and strengthen the prosecution of offenders. The Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah, said the operation would focus not only on illegal miners in the field but also on the networks and resources that enable their activities. Addressing the media with an update on the fight against illegal mining, he said intelligence gathering, field enforcement and investigations would be coordinated to ensure that evidence gathered during operations leads to effective legal action. “Our operational focus will continue to target the equipment, suppliers, and facilitators who sustain illegal mining operations,” he said. Colonel Appiah said the need for close cooperation between operational teams, investigators and prosecutors, saying that enforcement efforts must be backed by effective investigations and legal proceedings. “Intelligence, field enforcement, and investigations must support one another. And we are going to cooperate with investigators and prosecutors to translate evidence into effective legal action,” he said. He added that professionalism, accountability and public trust would remain central to the work of NAIMOS as it continues its operations against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. Colonel Appiah said personnel deployed to tackle illegal mining had been directed to operate within their lawful authority, preserve evidence and treat suspects in accordance with the law. He said that discipline and integrity among officers were essential to the credibility and success of the operation. “On my part, I will say that professionalism and public trust are essential to our operational success,” he said. “I remain committed to accountability, integrity, and disciplined conduct,” he added. According to him, task forces operating in the field would be expected to uphold these standards while carrying out their duties. “Our personnel, the task forces in the field, will act within their authority, preserve evidence, and treat suspects lawfully,” he said. However, the operations director said that officers would defend themselves when confronted with hostile acts or clear hostile intent. “We’ll continue to reserve our right to self-defence against hostile acts and hostile intent,” he added. Colonel Appiah said the success of NAIMOS operations should not be judged solely by the number of raids conducted or illegal mining sites cleared. Instead, he said, the focus should be on whether cleared areas remained free from renewed illegal mining, whether such activities declined and whether cases progressed through the justice system. He also identified measurable environmental recovery as an important indicator of progress. “We must judge our progress by whether cleared areas remain secure, illegal activity declines, cases advance through the justice system, and environmental recovery becomes measurable,” he said. He added that NAIMOS would work closely with relevant environmental and water institutions to assess the impact of its operations and determine whether interventions were producing lasting results. Colonel Appiah identified community engagement as a key part of NAIMOS operations, saying residents and local authorities could help prevent illegal miners from returning to areas where enforcement teams had intervened. He said traditional authorities, district assemblies, landowners and residents all had important roles to play in supporting lawful activities and providing credible information about renewed encroachment. “One key aspect of our operations is community engagement. It is integral to our operations currently,” he said. According to him, NAIMOS has received a significant number of reports from members of the public over the past two months, including information about locations where illegal mining activities were suspected. He said some whistleblowers had provided GPS coordinates and contact details, enabling operational teams to identify locations and respond to potential threats. “And in the past two months, we’ve received a lot of whistleblowing from various quarters where people call, send GPS locations, provide points of contact, and we have sent teams to prevent illegal mining in certain areas,” he said. The reports, he explained, had helped the secretariat deploy teams to intervene in some locations and prevent illegal mining activities. Colonel Appiah urged the public to continue sharing credible information with NAIMOS to support its enforcement efforts. “And we call on the public to let us know. We will conduct our reconnaissance and deal with the situations as they come,” he said.

items.description: Esperanza Aguirre, expresidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, entra en una enorme sala de vistas de la Audiencia Nacional sobre las 10.15 de este jueves. La antigua baronesa del PP, que aún mantiene una enorme influencia en las filas conservadoras, camina de seguido hacia los magistrados del tribunal que enjuician a Ignacio González, quien fuera su mano derecha durante años y su sucesor en el cargo. Mientras ella deja el bolso en el banquillo de los acusados (a solo cinco asientos de su exsubordinado) y silencia el móvil, él evita mirarla a la cara y centra la vista en un cuaderno de notas en blanco. items.title: NAIMOS vows to sustain crackdown on illegal mining in rivers, forests and farms
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has reaffirmed its determination to halt illegal mining in Ghana’s rivers, forests, farms and plantations, declaring that operations against illegal miners and the networks supporting them will continue. Colonel Appiah said the Secretariat’s efforts were directed not only at illegal miners operating at mining sites but also at the networks that sustain their activities. The Secretariat’s position comes amid concerns about the environmental and economic consequences of illegal mining, including damage to water bodies, forest reserves and agricultural lands. Mining activities in these areas threaten natural resources that support communities, farming and other livelihoods. “Our direction is clear. Mining in our rivers, forests, farms and plantations must stop,” Colonel K.S. Appiah, Director of Operations at NAIMOS, he said at a press conference at the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources on Thursday, October 22. By targeting both illegal mining operations and the networks behind them, NAIMOS is seeking to strengthen enforcement and protect environmentally sensitive areas from further degradation. Colonel Appiah reiterated that the objective was clear: to stop mining in rivers, forests, farms and plantations and sustain efforts against those responsible for the activities.

items.title: NDC records 137 aspirants for 14 positions ahead of 2026 national elections
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has closed nominations for its 2026 national executive elections, with 137 prospective aspirants picking forms to contest 14 positions ahead of the party’s 11th National Delegates Congress. The nomination-picking exercise ended at 5pm on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, paving the way for the next phase of the party’s internal electoral process. According to a statement from the party’s National Secretariat issued on Wednesday, October 21, all prospective aspirants have 14 days to complete their nomination forms, pay the relevant filing fees and secure the required endorsements in accordance with Sections 10 and 15 of the 2026 Guidelines for the Conduct of the National Congress. The National Executive Committee membership position attracted the highest number of prospective aspirants, with 53 applicants, followed by national vice-chairperson, which recorded 19. The deputy national organiser position attracted 14 applicants, while 11 picked forms to contest for deputy general secretary. Seven applicants each are seeking the positions of deputy national communication officer and national Zongo Caucus coordinator, while six are contesting for deputy national youth organiser. Five prospective aspirants picked forms for national chairman, while the national youth organiser and deputy national women organiser positions attracted four applicants each. The positions of general secretary, national communication officer and national women organiser recorded two applicants each. The national organiser position attracted one prospective aspirant. The party said the filing of completed nomination forms would take place from Saturday, November 7, to Monday, November 9, 2026, at its national headquarters in Adabraka, Accra. The exercise forms part of preparations for the NDC’s 11th National Delegates Congress, which will culminate in the election of the party’s national executives.

items.title: Faster reforms could triple Pakistan’s incomes by 2050, says World Bank
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s incomes could triple by 2050 if the country ensures faster implementation of structural reforms, according to the World Bank Group’s latest Pakistan Development Update, titled Attaining Escape Velocity. The report says that following progress on macroeconomic stabilisation, Pakistan has an opportunity to achieve faster and sustained economic growth and create more jobs. Sound macroeconomic policies in recent years have helped stabilise the economy and preserve growth despite the impact of the Middle East conflict . Real gross domestic product (GDP) growth increased to 3.7 per cent in FY26 from 3.2pc in FY25. Revenue growth and expenditure restraint supported record primary fiscal surpluses, which reached 2.9pc of GDP in FY26, while strong remittances enabled the country to rebuild its foreign exchange reserves. These improvements were recognised through upgrades by two major international rating agencies, S&P and Moody’s , and enabled Pakistan to return to international debt markets with the issuance of a $3 billion Eurobond. “Pakistan has made real progress in restoring stability, and markets have taken notice,” World Bank Country Dir­ector Bolormaa Amgaa­baz­­ar said. “But real per capita growth — the rate at which the income of the average Pakistani increases — remains stuck at around 1.6pc. Reforms to drive faster growth are now urgently needed,” she added. The report finds that higher growth is possible if Pakistan follows the path taken by other successful countries in pursuing ambitious economic reforms. Upgrading policies and institutions to the standards of the average middle-income country could drive sustained annual growth of 6.2pc to 6.9pc, allowing Pakistan to reach Vietnam’s current income level by 2050. “With macro stabilisation achieved but fiscal resources and foreign exchange still tightly constrained, structural reform to encourage private investment is the necessary next step towards higher living standards,” said Sebastian Essl, the report’s lead author. “Achieving this kind of private-sector-led growth requires a plan, coordination, and committed reform implementation,” he added. The report outlines an ambitious set of reforms that could enable Pakistan to attain by 2050 the per capita income levels of countries currently at the upper-middle-income threshold. Many of the proposed measures build on reforms already underway. These include timely adjustments to power-sector tariffs, which helped reduce energy subsidies from 1.1pc of GDP in FY25 to 0.8pc in FY26, continued trade liberalisation under the National Tariff Policy and the recent privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA). Building on these measures, sustained progress will depend on further reforms to improve the business environment, overhaul the tax system, reduce the state’s presence in the economy and expand access to finance.

items.title: NACOC strengthens ties with Ivorian counterparts to combat illicit drug trafficking
items.description: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has engaged border security authorities in Côte d’Ivoire to strengthen cross-border cooperation and intensify efforts to combat illicit drug trafficking along the Elubo–Noé border. The engagement forms part of the Commission’s strategic measures to curb drug trafficking and related criminal activities along the Ghanaian border. During a working visit to the Elubo Border on Wednesday, October 21, NACOC Director-General, Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, called for closer collaboration and a strong working relationship between the security agencies of Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire to address the threat. NACOC’s Deputy Director-General, accompanied Maj Gen Obuba Mantey, the Director-General, and Lawyer Alexander Twum-Barimah, who is in charge of Enforcement, Control and Elimination, along with other members of the Commission’s management team. He appealed to the Ivorian border security authorities to sustain their cooperation with their Ghanaian counterparts in pursuit of the shared goal of suppressing illicit drug trafficking and related activities. The Director-General also assured the Ivorian authorities that NACOC and other state security agencies operating under the Elubo Border Security Committee (BORSEC) would continue to uphold the professional and ethical standards governing their work. “We appreciate the existing working relationship among both BORSEC authorities. For NACOC, we are committed to ensuring that the drug trafficking network is curtailed,” he said. Maj Gen Obuba Mantey stressed the importance of maintaining effective cooperation between the two countries, noting that coordinated efforts among border security agencies were essential to tackling cross-border drug trafficking. In response, the Commissioner of Customs at the Ivorian Border Post, Avon Tah Felix, commended the NACOC delegation for the visit, describing the engagement as an opportunity to build and maintain a constructive working relationship between the two countries. He assured the delegation that the Ivorian border authorities would continue to provide support in various ways to protect the interests of both countries.

items.title: Formulate anti-sexual harassment policies to ensure zero tolerance in hospitality sector – Prof Christopher Mensah
items.description: The Pro Vice-Chancellor of Ho Technical University, Prof Christopher Mensah, has advocated for hotels to formulate strict policies to ensure zero tolerance for sexual harassment and maltreatment in the hospitality sector. He asserted that these vices may lead to a shortfall in human resources and compromised working and educational environments, among other consequences. He said that failing to curb these unfortunate behaviours, which are bred mostly in training institutions, would affect the sector’s productivity and growth. Prof Mensah was speaking at his inaugural lecture at the G.M. Afeti Auditorium of Ho Technical University, themed “Hidden curriculum toxic socialisation in Ghana’s higher education and hospitality sectors”. Academic portfolio Prof Christopher Mensah, a professor of Hospitality and Tourism Management, obtained his Bachelor of Science in Tourism in 1999 and his M.Phil. in Tourism in 2007 from the University of Cape Coast. He joined Ho Technical University in 2008, rose through the ranks, became an associate professor in 2020 and was subsequently promoted to the rank of professor in March 2025, with 65 peer-reviewed publications, among other achievements, to his credit. Sexual harassment and maltreatment are global phenomena In his inaugural address, Prof Christopher Mensah indicated that sexual harassment and maltreatment are global phenomena, with recorded occurrences in educational institutions and tourism and hospitality facilities. He said that date requests were the most common form of sexual harassment and maltreatment recorded, followed by uncomfortable touching, sexual conversation, requests for sexual favours, attempts to kiss or fondle, rewards promised for sex, faster promotion in exchange for sex, and threats of dismissal. He further indicated that records showed that guests were most likely to sexually harass workers in the hospitality and tourism sector, while co-workers and supervisors were also responsible for a proportion of harassment cases. He asserted that individuals begin learning the habit of using power to bully or coerce their subordinates into doing their bidding in training institutions. He used the lecturer-student relationship as a case study, recounting how some lecturers use their authority to make sexual demands, coupled with threats of academic failure, among other forms of coercion. Recommended approach for universities Prof Christopher Mensah called on lecturers to cultivate the habit of teaching authoritatively, without verbal abuse, aggression or excessively high standards, among other harmful practices. He also entreated university management to reform examination guidelines by introducing transparent marking schemes, providing options for second marking and establishing a fair appeals system. He called for guidelines to restrict lecturers from requesting personal services from students, establish robust reporting, investigation and accountability structures, and ensure “regular climate surveys; counselling; staff development.” “Mistreatment and harassment are common in Ghana’s universities and hospitality workplaces, and are sustained by power, dependency and silence rather than by a few individuals. Hospitality students meet them earlier and more often, mostly from those who teach them. Universities carry a double responsibility: to prepare students for the industry, and to stop passing on its worst habits”, he said. Recommended approach for hotels Prof Mensah advocated that hotel management introduce and display policies emphasising the facility’s zero tolerance for sexual harassment and maltreatment. “The hotel management must adopt and display a policy that states the hotel’s position on zero tolerance with posters and leaflets in all areas”, he said. He also suggested training complaints-handling staff to act on complaints, including those from and about guests, while protecting young women working in reception and food and beverage areas, as they are more vulnerable to harassment. He said another essential measure was to reduce reliance on tips by paying approved minimum wages to provide workers with financial security. Recommended approach for the Ghana Tourism Authority Prof Mensah entreated the Ghana Tourism Authority to make anti-harassment policy a requirement for licensing or renewals, urging it to support lower-star hotels in developing such policies. He also called on the authority to enforce the payment of the minimum wage to hotel staff and train staff in how to prevent and report sexual harassment and maltreatment. Call to students He entreated students not to let anyone trample on their rights, to use trusted channels to report sexual harassment and to keep records of such incidents, including dates, places and witnesses. “Support your peers; speak up when you see mistreatment/sexual harassment. Break the cycle; when you hold power, do not repeat what you suffered”, he counselled. The Vice-Chancellor of Ho Technical University, Prof Ben Honyenuga, eulogised Prof Christopher Mensah for his contribution to shaping hospitality and tourism education and the sector. “Prof Mensah has made significant contributions to advance fields including Tourism Development, Hospitality Management, and Human Resource Management, academic integrity, and sustainable tourism management, employee well-being, student development and industry resilience”, he listed, among other contributions.

items.title: NBA : Mouhamed Gueye vise un retour fin novembre après sa fracture au pied
items.description: Les Atlanta Hawks devront encore patienter avant de retrouver Mouhamed Gueye. L'intérieur sénégalais, absent depuis le début de la saison, pourrait refouler les parquets autour du 20 novembre 2026. Tout remonte au 8 juillet dernier. À l'entraînement, le joueur de 23 ans s'est fracturé le pied gauche. Il a été opéré le 14 juillet à Atlanta, et depuis, la franchise de Géorgie suit de près l'évolution de sa convalescence. Cette échéance de fin novembre n'est cependant qu'une estimation : elle doit encore être confirmée officiellement par le club. Gueye avait pourtant bien compté la saison passée dans la rotation des Hawks. Il avait pris part à 77 rencontres, pour 4,4 points et 3,6 rebonds de moyenne en 15,3 minutes par match. Le Sénégalais poursuit aujourd'hui sa rééducation, avec l'espoir d'être de retour avant la fin du mois de novembre. Son calendrier dépendra toutefois de l'évolution de sa condition physique et de la décision du staff médical d'Atlanta. O.B.N

items.title: Égypte : un soutien militaire à Riyad, mais sans attaque au Yémen
items.description: L'egypte veut aider l'Arabie saoudite face aux attaques houthies, mais en fixant une ligne rouge : aucune frappe egyptienne n'est prevue au Yemen. Le president egyptien Abdel Fattah al-Sissi a precise le 21 octobre que l'eventuel engagement militaire du Caire serait strictement limite a la defense du territoire et des frontieres saoudiennes. « Je ne parle pas d'affronter ou d'attaquer qui que ce soi », avait-il deja insiste le 17 octobre. Concretement, l'aide envisagee pourrait prendre la forme de moyens de defense antiaerienne et antimissile, de systemes anti-drones, de partage de renseignement, d'escorte navale ou encore d'un soutien logistique. L'objectif serait donc de permettre a Riyad d'intercepter les missiles et drones houthis visant ses villes, ses aeroports et ses infrastructures petrolieres, sans participer aux bombardements saoudiens sur Sanaa ou d'autres zones controlees par les Houthis. Le precedent des annees 1960 La prudence egyptienne s'explique aussi par l'histoire. Dans les annees 1960, l'egypte du president Gamal Abdel Nasser avait envoye des dizaines de milliers de soldats au Yemen et subi de lourdes pertes. Ce passe reste tres present au Caire, qui veut eviter d'etre aspire dans une nouvelle guerre terrestre longue et coûteuse. Politiquement, l'egypte affiche neanmoins un soutien tres fort a Riyad. Son Conseil national de defense a approuve le 18 octobre « toutes les formes de soutien necessaires et possibles » pour proteger la securite et l'integrite territoriale saoudiennes. Le Parlement doit encore se prononcer le 26 octobre sur l'autorisation d'un eventuel engagement militaire, conformement a la Constitution. Le Caire envoie donc un message double : il voit en l'Arabie saoudite un partenaire strategique dont la securite fait partie de la securite nationale arabe, mais refuse pour l'instant de transformer sa solidarite en intervention offensive contre les Houthis.

Ministres et députés... les règles constitutionnelles qui encadrent la vacance des sièges au Parlement
items.description: La nomination de parlementaires au sein du nouveau gouvernement entraîne l’application des règles d’incompatibilité entre mandat législatif et fonction gouvernementale. La procédure fait intervenir la Cour constitutionnelle pour les sièges à la Chambre des représentants, avant le remplacement des élus concernés par les candidats suivants sur les listes électorales. Plusieurs sièges sont ainsi appelés à changer de titulaires au sein des deux Chambres du Parlement. La formation du nouveau gouvernement dirigé par Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri entraîne une série de conséquences institutionnelles au Parlement. Plusieurs membres du nouvel Exécutif avaient été élus députés lors des élections législatives du 23 septembre 2026. Leur nomination à des fonctions gouvernementales les place dans une situation d’incompatibilité prévue par la législation marocaine, qui ne permet pas de cumuler la qualité de membre du gouvernement et le mandat de député. Le mécanisme applicable repose notamment sur la loi organique n° 27.11 relative à la Chambre des représentants. Celle-ci définit les situations d’incompatibilité, les modalités de constatation de la vacance d’un siège et les conditions dans lesquelles un autre candidat peut être appelé à remplacer le député concerné. Selon les informations relatives à la nouvelle composition gouvernementale, 13 sièges parlementaires sont concernés : 12 à la Chambre des représentants et un à la Chambre des conseillers. Ces changements découlent de la nomination de plusieurs élus au gouvernement, mais aussi de l’application des règles propres à chacune des deux Chambres. Incompatibilité entre le mandat parlementaire et la fonction gouvernementale L’article 14 de la loi organique n° 27.11 établit clairement l’incompatibilité entre la qualité de membre de la Chambre des représentants et celle de membre du gouvernement. Lorsqu’un député est nommé ministre, son maintien au sein de la première Chambre ne peut donc se poursuivre dans les mêmes conditions. La procédure prévoit l’intervention de la Cour constitutionnelle. Sur demande du président de la Chambre des représentants, celle-ci peut déclarer vacant le siège du député nommé au gouvernement, dans un délai d’un mois. Cette étape permet de formaliser juridiquement la vacance du siège. Elle ne doit pas être confondue avec le remplacement du parlementaire, qui obéit à une autre disposition de la loi organique. L’article 17 du même texte prévoit par ailleurs la déchéance de plein droit du mandat du député qui accepte, en cours de mandat, une fonction incompatible avec celui-ci, ou qui enfreint certaines dispositions légales. Ces règles participent à l’encadrement du statut des élus et à la prévention des situations de cumul interdit. 30 jours pour régulariser certaines situations La loi organique ne se limite pas à définir les incompatibilités. Son article 15 encadre également les situations dans lesquelles un élu se trouve dans une position incompatible avec son mandat. Il prévoit notamment que le parlementaire concerné doit régulariser sa situation dans un délai de 30 jours à compter de la proclamation des résultats définitifs des élections ou, en cas de contestation, de la décision de la Cour constitutionnelle. Cette régularisation passe par la démission des fonctions incompatibles avec le mandat parlementaire ou, lorsque cela est prévu, par une demande de mise en détachement. À défaut de régularisation dans les conditions prévues par la loi, l’élu s’expose à la cessation de son mandat parlementaire. Le même article impose également aux députés de déclarer auprès du bureau de la Chambre toute nouvelle activité professionnelle qu’ils envisagent d’exercer pendant la durée de leur mandat. Cette obligation permet de vérifier si l’activité concernée est compatible avec leur statut parlementaire. L’article 20 complète ce dispositif en interdisant aux députés d’utiliser leur nom, ou d’autoriser son utilisation en association avec leur qualité parlementaire, dans des publicités ou des annonces commerciales liées à des sociétés ou à des entreprises, quelle que soit la nature de leurs activités. L’ensemble de ces dispositions vise à encadrer l’exercice du mandat et à prévenir les conflits entre les responsabilités parlementaires et d’autres fonctions ou activités. Comment les sièges vacants sont-ils attribués ? Une fois la vacance d’un siège constatée, son remplacement est organisé conformément aux règles électorales. L’article 90 de la loi organique n° 27.11 prévoit que, pour les sièges attribués au scrutin de liste, le candidat dont le nom suit immédiatement celui du dernier élu sur la liste concernée est appelé à occuper le siège vacant. Cette substitution n’est toutefois pas automatique au seul motif qu’un candidat figure en deuxième position. La procédure prévoit une vérification du maintien des conditions d’éligibilité du candidat appelé à remplacer le député sortant, ainsi que l’accomplissement des formalités nécessaires. Le mécanisme permet de préserver la représentation des électeurs au Parlement sans imposer systématiquement l’organisation d’un nouveau scrutin dans la circonscription concernée. Les remplaçants annoncés à la Chambre des représentants Parmi les sièges concernés figurent ceux de plusieurs membres du gouvernement issus du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), du Parti de l’Istiqlal, de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) et du Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS). À Marrakech-Sidi Youssef Ben Ali, Mohamed Idrissi est appelé à remplacer Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, élue dans cette circonscription avant sa nomination à la tête du gouvernement. À Taroudant-Nord, Mehdi Oudal est annoncé comme remplaçant d’Abdellatif Ouahbi, reconduit au ministère de la Justice. À Casablanca-Anfa, Moulay Youssef Alaoui El Mohammedi est appelé à succéder à Naouja Koukous, nommée ministre de la Famille, du Développement social et de l’Égalité. D’autres changements sont annoncés dans les rangs du Parti de l’Istiqlal. À Larache, Abdelalam El Hana doit remplacer Nizar Baraka, nommé ministre de l’Équipement, de l’Eau et des Forêts. À Benslimane, Yassine Tariki est appelé à succéder à Ryad Mezzour, qui conserve le portefeuille de l’Industrie, du Commerce, de l’Investissement et de l’Intégration économique. À Rabat-Océan, Mohamed Majid Kheloua est annoncé pour remplacer Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid, nommé ministre de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et des Sports. À Rehamna, Abdelatif Zaïm doit retrouver son siège à la Chambre des représentants à la suite de la nomination d’Ezzedine El Midaoui à la tête du département de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche scientifique et de l’Innovation. Le Parti du progrès et du socialisme doit également être concerné par ces changements. À Boulemane, Noureddine Loukil est annoncé comme remplaçant de Rachid Hamouni, nommé ministre délégué chargé de l’Intégration sociale. À Zagora, El Madani Chikhi est appelé à succéder à Abderrahim Chahid, devenu ministre de l’Emploi et du Dialogue social. D’autres remplacements sont annoncés dans les circonscriptions de Taroudant-Nord, Oujda-Angad et Béni Mellal. À Taroudant-Nord, Abderrahmane El Ounissi doit remplacer Abdessamad Qaiouh, nommé ministre du Transport et de la Logistique. À Oujda-Angad, Mohamed Zine est appelé à succéder à Omar Hjira, nommé ministre délégué chargé du Commerce extérieur. À Béni Mellal, Lahcen Oualkadi est annoncé comme remplaçant de Madiha Khiyer, qui avait été nommée ministre déléguée chargée de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification avant d’être relevée de ses fonctions gouvernementales. Ces noms correspondent aux candidats annoncés comme successeurs des élus concernés. Leur prise de fonction doit être distinguée de la procédure juridique de constatation de la vacance et de validation du remplacement. Un siège également concerné à la Chambre des conseillers Les changements ne se limitent pas à la Chambre des représentants. La nomination de Fatima Saadi au poste de ministre déléguée chargée de l’Habitat et de la Politique de la ville entraîne également une procédure concernant son siège à la Chambre des conseillers. Selon les informations relatives à la nouvelle composition gouvernementale, Abdelaziz Benazzouz, président de l’arrondissement de Mghogha à Tanger, est appelé à lui succéder au sein de cette institution. Le cas de la Chambre des conseillers doit toutefois être distingué de celui de la première Chambre. La loi organique n° 27.11 et ses articles relatifs à la vacance des sièges concernent spécifiquement les députés de la Chambre des représentants. La procédure applicable aux conseillers relève des dispositions propres à cette institution et au mode de désignation ou d’élection du siège concerné. Le remplacement des parlementaires nommés au gouvernement répond ainsi à un mécanisme juridique qui articule plusieurs étapes : constatation de l’incompatibilité, intervention des autorités compétentes, déclaration de vacance du siège et désignation du candidat appelé à remplacer l’élu. Cette procédure vise à garantir le respect des règles encadrant les fonctions publiques tout en assurant la continuité de la représentation parlementaire. La nomination d’un député au gouvernement ne suffit donc pas, à elle seule, à achever le processus : les effets sur son siège et l’arrivée de son remplaçant doivent être établis conformément aux textes en vigueur. The post Ministres et députés... les règles constitutionnelles qui encadrent la vacance des sièges au Parlement appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: State appeals Court of Appeal ruling suspending Hanan’s trial over charge sheet dispute
items.description: The State has appealed to the Supreme Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision to suspend the criminal trial of former Buffer Stock CEO Hanan Aludiba and his wife, Faiza Seidu. Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, announced the appeal in a Facebook post on Thursday, October 22, 2026, saying it was filed on Wednesday, October 21. The appeal follows the Court of Appeal’s decision on Monday, October 19, to halt proceedings at the High Court pending the determination of Hanan Aludiba’s challenge to alleged defects in the charge sheet. Hanan Aludiba and his wife stand trial on multiple charges, including stealing, defrauding by false pretences, wilfully causing financial loss to the Republic, using public office for profit, dishonestly receiving, and money laundering. The High Court dismissed Hanan’s application to strike out the charge sheet in July 2026. He subsequently appealed that decision and sought a stay of proceedings, which the Court of Appeal granted on October 19. Dr Srem-Sai argued that a criminal trial should not be suspended simply because an accused person has raised objections to charges, particularly where those objections have already been dismissed as lacking merit. “The law does not allow a criminal trial to be suspended simply because an Accused Person has complained about some of the charges on the charge sheet, more so when those complaints were dismissed as meritless,” he stated. The Deputy Attorney-General said the state was challenging the suspension because of its implications for the prosecution of criminal cases. The appeal seeks to overturn the Court of Appeal’s order. The Supreme Court has not announced a date to hear the matter. The state’s appeal is the latest development in the procedural dispute over the charges and whether the High Court trial can proceed while Hanan’s appeal is pending.

items.title: Cybersécurité : la DGSSI émet une alerte critique sur deux failles majeures affectant PHP au Maroc et à l'international
items.description: Une alerte mondiale de niveau critique a été déclenchée ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026 suite à la découverte de deux vulnérabilités majeures au sein de PHP, l'un des langages de programmation les plus répandus pour l'administration des sites web et des systèmes de gestion de contenu comme WordPress, Drupal ou Joomla. Au Maroc, la Direction générale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (DGSSI), rattachée à l'Administration de la Défense nationale, a publié le jour même un bulletin de sécurité classant l'impact et le risque au niveau maximal. Référencées sous les codes CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619, ces deux failles regroupées sous l'appellation « PHP2Shell » affichent chacune un score de gravité de 9,2 sur 10 sur l'échelle internationale CVSS. La menace est jugée d'autant plus urgente qu'un code de démonstration (PoC) permettant leur exploitation est déjà accessible publiquement, ouvrant la voie à des tentatives d'intrusion ciblées. Selon la DGSSI, les failles permettent à des cybercriminels d'exécuter du code malveillant à distance sans authentification préalable, d'accéder à des données confidentielles et de prendre le contrôle de serveurs vulnérables. L'alerte touche plusieurs environnements techniques, notamment les configurations utilisant PHP-FPM, Apache avec mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP ou LiteSpeed. Face au risque immédiat d'attaques, des mesures conservatoires ont été observées à l'échelle internationale, avec la mise en maintenance préventive et l'interruption temporaire de plusieurs plateformes web publiques et privées, notamment en France. L'équipe de sécurité de PHP a publié le 21 octobre des correctifs d'urgence correspondant aux versions PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 et 8.5.12. La DGSSI exhorte les administrateurs de systèmes d'information au Maroc à déployer ces mises à jour sans délai, tout en recommandant la migration impérative des installations opérant sous des versions obsolètes telles que PHP 8.1 ou antérieures, qui ne disposent plus de support officiel. items.title: Marché de Matoto : Mohamed Soumah entendu au commissariat, les commerçants menacent de remobiliser
items.description: La tension reste vive au marché de Matoto. Après la manifestation organisée lundi par des vendeurs et vendeuses contre le marquage de leurs boutiques et magasins, Mohamed Soumah, l’un des manifestants, a été entendu ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026 au commissariat central de Matoto. En réaction, plusieurs commerçants se sont mobilisés sur place et menacent de reprendre la rue dès ce jeudi matin. À l’origine de la protestation, le marquage de plusieurs boutiques et magasins, accompagné d’une injonction de libérer les lieux dans un délai de 72 heures. Les commerçants concernés affirment ignorer l’identité des auteurs de cette opération. Ils indiquent également avoir sollicité des explications auprès du bureau du marché et de la mairie, sans obtenir de réponse claire sur les motifs de cette mesure. Estimant être visés par une opération de déguerpissement annoncée sans préavis formel, les vendeurs et vendeuses ont exprimé leur mécontentement à travers une manifestation dans l’enceinte du marché. Ce mercredi, l’affaire a connu un nouveau développement avec la plainte visant Mohamed Soumah en lien avec cette mobilisation. Selon ses déclarations à notre rédaction, des personnes se sont présentées à son domicile avant de le conduire au commissariat central de Matoto. « Ils ont porté plainte contre moi. Les gens sont venus chez moi pour me conduire au commissariat central de Matoto. C’est en rapport avec la manifestation du marché. Mais pour les détails, je n’ai aucune idée. Je dois me présenter là-bas. À l’heure où nous sommes, je suis en route pour là-bas », avait-il confié. Informés de sa présence au commissariat, plusieurs commerçants s’y sont rendus pour s’enquérir de sa situation. Sur place, des agents leur ont expliqué que leur camarade n’était pas en détention, mais qu’il était entendu au sujet des événements survenus lundi au marché. Après des échanges avec les forces de l’ordre, les commerçants ont finalement accepté de quitter les lieux pour retourner au marché et poursuivre leurs activités. Toutefois, le calme reste précaire. Les manifestants menacent d’organiser une nouvelle mobilisation dès ce jeudi matin et de barricader le passage si Mohamed Soumah n’est pas libéré dans la soirée de ce mercredi. Au moment de la mise en ligne de cet article, Mohamed Soumah se trouvait toujours dans les locaux du commissariat central de Matoto pour son audition. Selon des sources policières, il n’était pas en détention et n’avait pas été placé au violon. Mayi Cissé L’article Marché de Matoto : Mohamed Soumah entendu au commissariat, les commerçants menacent de remobiliser est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
